items.claim: U9 pre-65 healthcare-gap line is a special, income-dependent slot (the seam to U11): the budget RESERVES the time-boxed slot (retirement→65 per spouse, Medicare being individual) but its NET COST is computed by the Act-1 U3 overlay (ACA premium − PTC, MAGI-dependent), surfaced through U11 — NOT a user-typed flat amount, or the model would silently miss the conversion↔subsidy interaction. The gap line is `tier: 'essentials'` (you cannot go uninsured pre-65 — part of the survival floor, counted in Tier-1), one window per spouse ending at that spouse's age 65. Because the dollar is MAGI-dependent and the two tracks spend differently, it resolves to a PER-TRACK value — the essentials-only track's lower spend yields lower MAGI, more PTC, and a lower net premium than the full track; U3 computes its dollar inside each track's own MAGI fixed point.

items.claim: U9 Two-track compilation (the structural realization of the two-tier reading): `budgetToSpending` emits TWO per-year spending vectors from one budget — an essentials-only track (Tier-1 floor) and a full track (essentials + discretionary). The engine evaluates BOTH thresholds against the SAME path population on the SAME single shared draw set (contract #2): 'essentials covered every year' (Tier-1) and 'full lifestyle covered every year' (Tier-2). ONE shared draw set but TWO decumulation + overlay passes — essentials-only and full are DISTINCT portfolio trajectories, never the full-spend run read twice. This is the engine half of R21's lexicographic structure the Act-4 solver later optimizes (objective ≡ headline metric); U9 builds the *reading*, Act 4 builds the *objective over it*.

U9 Two-tier headline reading is NOT a 7th state: the headline composes TWO outcome-state-tagged readings over the SAME engine-owned SIX-state enum (Act-2 U7) — an essentials-floor verdict + a lifestyle-surplus verdict ('your essentials are safe in 10 of 10 futures; your full lifestyle holds in 7'). Negative-tier copy is action-first / Kitces ('in the other 3 you'd trim discretionary, not go hungry'); non-color signal grammar carries each tier's state independently. State-SELECTION stays engine-owned in `confidence.ts`; `TwoTierHeadline.tsx` is a pure presentation composition of two already-tagged states. DEGENERATE COLLAPSE: when the full track is byte-identical to the essentials track (no discretionary present), `TwoTierHeadline` renders the SINGLE-metric statement verbatim, not two identical tier verdicts — this is precisely what keeps the reduce-to-spine headline byte-identical.

U9 Spending shape is user-set, NEVER solver-recommended: a go-go-years front-load is a user-set per-year multiplier on the DISCRETIONARY track only (the solver optimizes *funding*, not how you live). U9 owns the shape control and surfaces its honest consequence on the surplus tier; it never proposes a shape.

U9 Reduce-to-spine invariant (the budget's golden anchor): a budget that is a SINGLE LIFELONG ESSENTIALS LINE equal to the first-answer total-spend figure must compile to the EXACT single per-year spending vector the first answer fed the engine → the saved seed/headline is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the single-total-spend answer. The single-total-spend answer IS the degenerate budget; itemization is the deepening, never the on-ramp (R5/R8). Migrating single-total → itemized preserves the seed.

U9 Survivor-spending composition (the seam to the survivor floor — R17, the product's emotional core): the survivor-spending ratio (the Act-1 U1 default) is applied PER-PATH at the sampled first death to the compiled tracks: it scales the DISCRETIONARY track and the DISCRETIONARY PORTION OF ESSENTIALS ONLY — STICKY SURVIVAL ESSENTIALS (the survivor's healthcare-gap / single-enrollee Medicare premium, housing, property tax) do NOT scale by the couple ratio, so the Tier-1 survivor floor is never silently understated. DEGENERATE-INERT: in the degenerate single-essentials-line budget the composition is inert (the ratio falls back to flat-on-total) so survivor-year vectors stay byte-identical. The composition lives in `budgetToSpending`, NOT `simulate`, and is surfaced as an R7-editable assumption (U12). A simpler ratio-on-total reading is the DOCUMENTED FALLBACK if the cold-read finds the split too fiddly.

U9 Files — Create: `src/budget/budgetModel.ts` (line-item shape + tier + time-box window), `src/budget/budgetToSpending.ts` (compiles itemized budget → the TWO per-year spending vectors the engine reads), `src/ui/BudgetBuilder.tsx`, `src/ui/BudgetLineItem.tsx`, `src/ui/TwoTierHeadline.tsx`. Modify: `src/shared/model.ts` (the `budget` field, under the single schemaVersion bump — contract #5), `src/store/memoryModel.ts` (budget edit → recompute), `src/ui/copy.ts` (two-tier headline + line-item strings). Test: `src/budget/__tests__/budgetModel.test.ts`, `budgetToSpending.test.ts`, `src/ui/__tests__/budgetBuilder.test.tsx`.

U9 Tier-ordering monotonicity (golden invariant): for any budget, Tier-1 (essentials) X-of-10 ≥ Tier-2 (full) X-of-10, asserted PATH-FOR-PATH on the shared draw set (every full-success path is an essentials-success path). The two tracks are distinct trajectories with different MAGI, so this is NOT assumed — it rests on a three-link proof chain: (1) essentials-only spend ≤ full spend every year; (2) on identical CRN draws, depletion is monotone in spend (less spent ⇒ never-lower balances); (3) the per-track healthcare-gap dollar is itself monotone in spend (lower spend → lower MAGI → ≥ PTC → ≤ net premium → ≤ cash need). The three links compose. HONEST CAVEAT: if any link can break (a cliff/CSR branch where a lower MAGI crosses into a regime that RAISES a different cost), the invariant is NARROWED to the region where it provably holds and the exception is documented, never asserted universally and left to block a correct engine. Pair the subset-assert with a presence companion that ≥1 path stressed the discretionary gap (`burned/027`); a planted budget whose two passes diverge inside the proven region fails loud.

U9 key test scenarios: (a) reduce-to-spine edge — a single lifelong essentials line = first-answer total → compiled vector byte-identical under same seed, survivor-spending composition INERT (flat-on-total), rendered headline is SINGLE-metric form not a doubled tier pair; (b) two-tier split over one draw — essentials safe 10/10 while full holds 7/10, both read off the SAME path population/draw set (assert IDENTICAL normals consumed), not two sims; (c) real-convention — a constant-real multi-year line compiles to the engine's expected REAL per-year vector not nominally-flat; (d) income-dependent gap line — the gap dollar comes from the overlay (U11) not a typed amount, removing the gap line does not zero a typed value; (e) zero-essentials coherent-but-warned — all-discretionary yields a trivially-safe floor with calm warning, never error/indeterminate; (f) R19 errors — negative amount and endYear<startYear caught calmly inline.

U9 Verification + exit condition: a user builds a real itemized time-boxed budget; the answer reads as two honest tiers over the same state set; a single-total budget reproduces the first answer byte-identically; spending shape is user-set with honest consequences never recommended. PASSING THE N=1 COLD-READ ON THE TWO-TIER HEADLINE (relief-with-honesty, not two competing verdicts) is an Act-3 EXIT CONDITION (contract #8). Feeds forward: the two-tier essentials/surplus split IS the lexicographic objective's two tiers; the budget is READ-ONLY input to the solver (it never moves a budget line). See docs/plans/4-recommendation.md contracts #4 and #8a.

U9 The two-date split rides this unit — NO new budget mechanism. The fuck-off date's floor vs lifestyle dates (R27) are this unit's two-track compilation consumed by the date-search (C3, shipped in Act 1): the two dates COINCIDE in the degenerate single-total-spend case via this unit's existing degenerate-collapse, and SEPARATE when the budget splits the tracks — C3 consumes whatever two tracks `budgetToSpending` emits; nothing in the date-search is rebuilt. The mixed date outcomes — `{floor: date, lifestyle: no-date}` and the `floor > lifestyle` 100%-FPL-floor signature — are DARK until this unit lands; the result *shape* already admits them from C3, the behavioral tests ride here.

The tax-aware baseline's sequencing policy is named explicitly — `proportional` (the neutral, tax-agnostic default) — and the sequencing control's two arms are the SELECTED-POLICY arm vs the BASELINE-POLICY arm on shared CRN draws (conversion held fixed). `bracket-fill` carries an explicit TARGET-BRACKET PARAMETER and a CLIFF-AWARE FILL CEILING (the subsidy-aware MAGI line pre-65 / the next IRMAA step post-65, per Act-1 U3), so contract #7's 'bracket headroom real' check is measured against that ceiling, never the nominal bracket top. In any post-RMD-age year the RMD is distributed from pre-tax as ordinary income FIRST and the conversion STACKS ON TOP — the conversion never reduces or satisfies the RMD, and the conversion clamp `[0, remaining pre-tax pool]` is computed AFTER the RMD is removed from the pool. items.claim: U12 Each edit re-runs through the Act-2 U5 `memoryModel` orchestrator (it EXTENDS, never re-owns, the recompute home) with the SAME seed → the answer MORPHS (draw-once-then-morph, never a re-draw) and the margin-gated crossfade Act 2 defined is EXERCISED here (Act 2 tested it only with synthetic recomputes).

U12 R8 honestly — 'sharpens,' not unconditionally 'tightens' (band-narrowing is mechanically true for only ONE edit class): (a) CONFIRM/NARROW an epistemic default (replace a wide conservative assumption with a more confident one) → the band genuinely NARROWS (R8's rewarding case); (b) OVERRIDE a value (real higher spending, a longer longevity table, a higher σ) → the band SHIFTS and may WIDEN, and the verdict can worsen — framed calmly as 'a truer picture,' never a failure. 'Monotonic, no jitter' is the SEED-STABILITY guarantee (same seed → no sampling noise), NOT a promise every edit narrows.

U12 This unit SEATS the stateful sticky-rounding (the seam Act-1 U1 + Act-2 U5 handed forward). It adds `lastDisplayedHeadline` / `lastDisplayedDollar` / `lastState` to `memoryModel` and the sticky rule, applied to edits of an ALREADY-COMPLETE answer: (a) TWO DISTINCT MARGINS — headline + `lastState` (copy-state / verb-tense) gate on the BAND-EDGE margin; `lastDisplayedDollar` gates on the INDEPENDENT DISPLAY-ROUNDING-STEP margin (conflating them is the 'one sticky while the other flickers in one sentence' failure); (b) NOTIFY-ONCE write ordering (`burned/017`) — one recompute writes all displayed slices + the `lastDisplayed*` stickiness BEFORE the single notify; (c) LIFECYCLE — the baseline is captured at the RESOLVE→VERDICT transition (free-moving while indeterminate); `lastDisplayed*` are SESSION-ONLY, NOT PERSISTED, re-seated on re-entry from U13's deterministic recompute, so the first post-unlock edit is sticky against the exact number the user last saw and a genuinely-moved answer (staleness) is never held to a stale screenshot value. (Why the stateful stickiness lives here, not in pure `confidence.ts`: architecture.md §9.)

items.claim: U12 Honest about the epistemic vs aleatory floor: sharpening narrows input uncertainty but cannot narrow market randomness — copy for 'you've hit the floor, more precision won't narrow it' and for 'sharpening revealed bad news' (real higher spending worsens the verdict — handled calmly). The worsening transition carries the non-color signal grammar (word + shape + dollar magnitude, never a hue shift — the reader is color blind) and is a cold-read subject (contract #8). FLOOR DETECTION (decided, MVP-minimal): a UNIT-12-LOCAL HEURISTIC — when an edit collapses an input's uncertainty toward a point and the band-width change is below a defined threshold, surface the floor copy. The alternative (a `confidence.ts` inputs-vs-returns decomposition emission) would re-open Act 1 and is DELIBERATELY NOT chosen for the MVP; escalate only if the cold-read finds the heuristic too coarse.

U12 Escape hatch: jump straight to any assumption without walking the guided path (R6), reachable EVEN WHILE the answer is INDETERMINATE — the sticky seam applies ONLY to a complete answer, so an escape-hatch edit on an indeterminate answer has defined (non-sticky) behavior (Act-2 U5's indeterminate render). PASSING THE N=1 COLD-READ ON THE BAD-NEWS SHARPEN TRANSITION (honest recalibration, not a gut-punch) is an Act-3 EXIT CONDITION. U13 — Returning-user re-entry + per-surface staleness goal: a calm re-entry that shows the saved answer (re-derived, not a replayed string) with honest, per-surface staleness awareness across the tax, healthcare, and budget clocks — and routes the surviving spouse back in. Requirements: R4 (the saved answer surface), R8 (re-entry, not re-intake), R15/R16/R17 (unlock + the survivor recovery door + the two-person posture).

U13 Unlock surfaces ALL of Act-1 U4's outcomes — including the survivor's primary door. ReEntry is the explicit consumer of Act-1 U4's FOUR outcomes: WRONG-PASSPHRASE → calm retry, no lockout; DATA-DAMAGED → 'use your export' restore; NO-VAULT / POST-EVICTION (Safari ~7-day) → restore as a first-class entry; and the IN-PLACE RECOVERY-PHRASE UNLOCK — forgotten passphrase + intact vault → unlock via the recovery phrase → set a new passphrase. The recovery door is the SURVIVING SPOUSE'S PRIMARY WAY BACK IN — the flow the product exists to serve. TWO SECURITY OBLIGATIONS (both MUST hold): (a) setting a new passphrase is a MANDATORY BLOCKING GATE — NO WRITE PATH IS REACHABLE until the new passphrase is set and the `passphraseWrap` re-minted (fresh salt+IV), or the survivor could save while the on-disk wrap still encodes the forgotten passphrase, silently degrading the vault to recovery-phrase-only access (the worst survivor outcome); (b) the recovery-phrase ENTRY FIELD is MASKED BY DEFAULT (reveal-on-hold), and any step that displays the phrase carries the same 'store offline, don't screenshot' instruction first-save uses. (The synchronous lock authority / write-gate conjunction is owned by architecture.md §7.3.)
items.sourceSection: Unit 13 — Unlock surfaces all U4 outcomes (line 256)

items.claim: U13 Show the saved confidence statement by RE-DERIVING it at unlock (not replaying a stored string): `memoryModel` recomputes the saved model under its PERSISTED SEED → byte-identical to the saved displayed value → and this RE-SEATS U12's session-only sticky baseline so the first post-unlock edit is sticky against the exact number the user last saw. RE-PRESENTATION uses the SAVED FIXTURE VINTAGE (so the number matches what the user screenshotted) with the staleness flag as the honest signal; any RE-RUN (entering the sharpen loop or re-opening a control) recomputes under the CURRENT fixture and explicitly states the assumptions were updated — never silently stale, never silently changed. FORWARD HAND TO ACT-4 U17: once a *recommendation* can be saved, a stale saved recommendation is a real EXECUTED ACTION and its staleness must INVERT to re-solve under current fixtures — 'the action we recommended may no longer be advised,' not 'your number drifted.' In Act 3 only the spine + the manual-control results are saved, so the re-present-under-saved-vintage rule holds — a saved MANUAL-CONTROL result stays a what-if (re-presented under its saved vintage), and ONLY a saved RECOMMENDATION inverts to re-solve-under-current (the boundary the reset turns on: a saved control what-if ≠ a saved executed action); U13 lays the per-surface clock groundwork U17 inherits.

U13 Per-surface multi-clock staleness (contract #6 — a clock exists IFF the engine consumes a year-stamped parameter, gates only its surface): (1) WALL-TIME SINCE LAST EDIT + APP METHODOLOGY-DEFAULT VINTAGE (new conservative-return/longevity defaults shipped since save AND never user-overridden → a calm 'we've updated our default assumptions' note; user-overridden assumptions immune) → gate the SPINE VERDICT. (2) TAX-TABLE VINTAGE (the bracket/standard-deduction fixture, carrying its OBBBA-2025 legal-basis as provenance) + RMD-AGE RULE (birth-year-derived; the legislated 73→75 step in 2033) + SENIOR-BONUS-DEDUCTION SUNSET (a calm note when a pre-2029 answer is viewed in/after 2029) → gate the CONTROLS/LEVER ONLY (the spine is tax-blind). SS provisional-income thresholds are frozen/not-indexed → NO clock. A saved control result is flagged stale when ANY of {bracket vintage, RMD-age rule, senior-bonus-deduction sunset} has moved; when stale and opened, the surface shows the vintage at the control ('computed with [year] tax brackets') and does not present the survivor-cliff figure as current — `staleness.ts` exposes a queryable 'tax-table stale' flag.

U13 Per-surface staleness clocks (continued): (3) HEALTHCARE VINTAGES (net-new) → gate the HEALTHCARE SURFACES: the ACA LEGISLATIVE STATUS (the load-bearing clock — cliff-on vs enhanced; the re-verify-at-build status), the APPLICABLE-% TABLE, the IRMAA BRACKETS, the PART B PREMIUM. A saved healthcare cost is flagged stale when any has moved; the ACA-status clock is the most consequential (it can flip the whole pre-65 calculus). (4) The UNDETECTABLE BALANCE-DRIFT CLOCK (real portfolio drifted; no aggregation): a calm 'is this still your balance?' confirm before presenting the saved verdict as current. FOR AN ACCOUNTS VAULT it confirms the PER-BUCKET SPLIT (pre-tax/Roth/taxable/HSA), not just the total — the pre-tax pool's drift relative to Roth changes the control calculus more than the total does; a CHANGED SPLIT routes into the U10 MINI-INTAKE, a CHANGED TOTAL into the U12 SHARPEN LOOP. SS staleness folded in as 'are these still your benefit amounts?' (SS benefits are user-entered, not a year-stamped fixture — no separate clock). (5) BUDGET TIME-BOXED CLOCKS (net-new) → gate the BUDGET SURFACE: a budget line whose WINDOW HAS ADVANCED since save (a travel item past its `endYear`; the pre-65 healthcare-gap item once a spouse reached 65) gets a calm RE-CONFIRM rather than silently spending past its window.

U13 The DATE ANSWER joins the per-surface staleness/re-entry machinery (the most time-denominated answer in the product would otherwise have no clock): (1) FIXTURE-VINTAGE CLOCKS gating the DATE surface: the CONTRIBUTION-LIMIT TABLE VINTAGE (answer-relevant not intake-only: the per-runway-year catch-up step-down shapes the projected stream, so a vintage move shifts the date) and the TICKER-BLEND / TDF STATIC-SNAPSHOT VINTAGE (a stale snapshot silently misstates the household stock weight). (2) USER-ENTERED RE-CONFIRMS ride the existing balance-drift confirm class, NEVER vintage clocks (the SS precedent): account values / contributions / salary join the 'is this still your balance?' confirm; the entered ACA QUOTE gets an 'is this still your marketplace quote?' PLAN-YEAR re-confirm (marketplace premiums reprice annually — user-entered, so a confirm not a fixture clock). (3) The DATE RE-PRESENTATION RULE: re-presentation renders the WALL-TIME-STABLE CALENDAR LABEL (`startCalendarYear + Y` — byte-identical under the saved vintage) and RE-DERIVES the relative '~N years out' framing from CURRENT WALL-TIME — never a replayed relative string (the date answer decays with pure time passage — ages advance against the saved t=0 anchor — so a sufficiently old save routes to RECOMPUTE via this unit's existing re-run rule, never re-presents as current). Act-4 U17's inverted stale-rec rule is unchanged (a saved recommendation still re-solves under current fixtures; the date is an answer, not an executed action).

inventories.label: plan-4-recommendation
inventories.oneLineRole: The Act-4 build plan for the solver + recommendation differentiator (Units 14-17): the validation-gated, held-out-seed, lexicographic-objective recommender that names a confidence-graded strategy over withdrawal-sequencing + Roth-conversion, plus its surface and stale-saved-recommendation handling.

items.claim: Act 4 is PLANNED, zero code: src/engine/solver/ and src/engine/validation/ are .gitkeep-only. This act is not started. The lifecycle front-matter (status: planned, created 2026-06-17) asserts this truthfully. This is the actual differentiator and is still entirely ahead.

The goal of Act 4: deliver the recommend-SECOND beat. After the spine's confidence statement (Act 2) and the user's budget + two manual controls (Act 3), the product recommends a confidence-graded strategy over two coupled controls — withdrawal SEQUENCING + Roth CONVERSION — that funds the user's budget toward the user's chosen goal. The solver ranks named drawdown policies x a conversion grid on identical Monte Carlo futures (CRN), selects a winner under a lexicographic objective whose metric IS the headline metric, reports confidence on a held-out seed-set, and surfaces the recommendation with its hedge on the headline, the runner-up retained, and the modeled omissions disclosed.

The validation harness that proves the recommendation is RIGHT is built and passing BEFORE the solver is allowed to recommend. The cardinal sin is calm-but-wrong on real money: a confidently-stated wrong recommendation costs real dollars and is worse than no tool. The recommender cannot speak until its correctness backstop (optimality oracle, ranking-stability under CRN, grade calibration, held-out-seed defense) exists and passes. "It's just for friends" must never soften this — friends risk identical real money with less protection and trust the tool more, so the validation bar RISES for a recommender.
items.sourceSection: The goal + Why this act lands last (lines 15, 17)

items.claim: Why Act 4 lands last: everything here CONSUMES the validated spine + the two deterministic overlays (Act 1) and the budget + manual controls (Act 3). The solver does not re-implement decumulation — it ranks candidate strategies through the exact same per-year cash-term transform seam the spine and manual controls already drive (docs/architecture.md §4).

The chain in one line: oracle -> solver -> surface -> staleness. U14 builds the validation harness whose compile-time oracle-cleared token gates U15; U15 runs named drawdown policies x a conversion grid on CRN under the lexicographic objective and emits a byte-identical winner + retained runner-up; U16 surfaces it as the recommend-second, confidence-graded comparative beat (objective ≡ headline, hedge-on-headline); U17 treats a stale saved recommendation as a real executed action and re-solves under current fixtures.

Pointers to canonical homes: the load-bearing invariants this act inherits (CRN/single shared market draw, reduce-to-spine byte-identity, externally-derived-fixture discipline, cross-engine headline-robustness quantization, worker boundary) live once in docs/architecture.md and are LINKED, not restated. The accumulation/fuck-off-date decision record is docs/decisions/accumulation-fuck-off-date.md. The lexicographic objective and lever set are locked in docs/product.md §4-§5.

CONTRACT #1 — Validation gates the solver (owned cross-cutting Units 14->15). Success criteria are two-tier: the engine's NUMBER is right (Trinity/Bengen golden cases, Act 1) AND the solver's RECOMMENDATION is right (Solver validation strand of docs/research/engine-validation-and-tax.md). Unit 14 is the second tier and GATES Unit 15: optimality/ranking oracle (hand-computable known-best cases), ranking-stability under CRN, and grade calibration must each exist and pass before the solver may emit a recommendation. Until the oracle passes, any solver output is DIRECTIONAL (marked so in code) and no Unit-16 surface may render it as a recommendation. The order is STRUCTURAL and TYPE-LEVEL not boolean: the 'oracle-cleared' result is an OPAQUE NOMINAL TOKEN constructable ONLY by the validation harness on a clean pass, and Unit 15's solve-as-recommendation entry point takes that token as a REQUIRED PARAMETER — so shipping a recommendation without a passing oracle is a TypeScript COMPILE error (mirroring Act 1's no-unkeyed-write seam). The gate's own test plants a wrong-best case the oracle must reject (burned/070). 'fixtures-pinned' is a CHECKED CLAUSE of the token: the harness mints the cleared token ONLY when every rec-relevant §Strand-5 + healthcare primary the near-ties depend on is pinned (directionalUntilPinned === false) AND ε is calibrated — a test plants a single still-directional rec-relevant constant (or uncalibrated-ε sentinel) and asserts the token is REFUSED.

CONTRACT #2 — Held-out-seed discipline: select on A, grade on B (owned by Unit 14; consumed by 15+16). Argmax over many candidates on a single seed overfits that seed's noise (the optimizer's curse); the in-sample winner's score is optimistically biased. Defense: SELECT the winning strategy on seed-set A, REPORT its graded confidence on independent held-out seed-set B. Both seed-sets are CRN-correct internally. A and B must be STATISTICALLY INDEPENDENT not merely distinct: seedA is the existing Act-2-minted scenario seed (so the spine headline still reproduces under it); seedB is derived by a HASH/SplitMix expansion of seedA into a well-separated stream — NEVER seedA+1 or a near-integer (whose mulberry32 streams correlate and silently make B optimistic). This is seed-INPUT decorrelation only; it does NOT replace mulberry32 as the path PRNG. Both seeds are first-class persisted model fields surviving encrypt->decrypt round-trip bit-identically (persist seedA + expanded seedB; no third master stored). The survival-equivalent ε has TWO DISTINCT ROLES that must not be conflated: the DISPLAY BAND (rendered uncertainty interval) measured on B; the SELECTION TIE-TOLERANCE that declares two candidates survival-equivalent is a selection decision and must NEVER be a B-measured level band. The selection tolerance is a pre-specified/theoretical standard error (or computed A-side), keyed to the variance of the pairwise DIFFERENCE between candidates under CRN (which CRN shrinks far below the variance of the level — a level-keyed band over-declares ties and can drop a survival-relevant gap into Tier-2). Pinning the §Strand-5 + healthcare primaries is a HARD solver PREREQUISITE, not a residual gate.

CONTRACT #3 — Deterministic, byte-identical recommendation selection (owned by Unit 15). The selected strategy + its grade + its runner-up must be byte-identical across reproductions and re-entry. Selection = a QUANTIZED objective (lexicographic score rounded to a stable display/decision granularity so float noise can't reorder near-ties) + a DETERMINISTIC LEXICOGRAPHIC TIE-BREAK (fixed candidate ordering: policy enum order, then conversion amount, then years) + a SEEDED SUB-STREAM ORTHOGONAL to the simulation draws (a THIRD stream, never one of seed-sets A/B, used only where a tie-break needs a deterministic coin — never for simulation). No Math.random, no clock, no getRandomValues inside the solver (engine-purity lint of Act 1 forbids them in src/engine/**). The selection is reproducible from (model, seedA, seedB, goal) alone. Byte-identical is a SAME-JS-ENGINE guarantee: the selection run and the held-out-B grade for one recommendation must execute on the SAME ENGINE INSTANCE, never a precomputed cross-engine baseline, or a single ULP delta in one Math.exp could reorder a near-tie and silently bias the grade.

CONTRACT #4 — Objective ≡ headline metric, lexicographic (owned by Unit 15 for objective; Unit 16 for render). The objective is LEXICOGRAPHIC (R21): Tier 1 (the floor) = the survival-floor statistic (essentials covered every year across futures) expressed in the spine's 'X of 10' natural-frequency metric; Tier 2 (the user picks) = a surplus goal, each a concrete distributional statistic the headline renders directly: PAY LESS TAX = lifetime tax paid (real dollars); LEAVE MORE = the bequest measured AFTER-TAX TO HEIRS — gross estate adjusted by a FIRST-ORDER §1014/IRD treatment (taxable basis stepped up at death, inherited pre-tax taxed as ordinary income-in-respect-of-a-decedent at a DISCLOSED ASSUMED HEIR BRACKET, Roth tax-free), NEVER gross/pre-heir-tax (a gross objective can crown the strategy that leaves LESS after-tax); LIVE BIGGER NOW = the held-out 'X of 10' confidence that the user's chosen front-loaded (go-go-years) discretionary spending shape holds across futures — a confidence-over-FIXED-spending statistic, NEVER a spend-amount the solver raises (budget stays read-only; telling the user how much MORE they could sustainably spend is a continuous-spending/die-with-zero solver, explicitly chapter-two). The quantity the solver maximizes IS the quantity the headline shows. When survival is a given the headline pivots (contract #6) to the SAME Tier-2 quantity the solver optimized. Candidates within the SELECTION tie-tolerance (CRN-difference-keyed, computed at selection, never B-measured display band) are survival-equivalent; among them the winner is the best Tier-2 score. Seed-set B carries the displayed number + grade, NEVER the choice of which candidates are survival-equivalent. Spending shape is never an objective term (contract #8) — the solver optimizes FUNDING, not how you live.

items.claim: CONTRACT #5 — Single shared market draw per year, now MORE load-bearing (owned by Unit 15). All account buckets (pre-tax/Roth/taxable/HSA) share ONE market-return draw per year; buckets differ only in tax treatment, never in return assumption. This lets the solver rank K candidate strategies on identical futures (signal, not luck) and structurally forecloses asset-location. Act 3 proved this for a 2-arm Roth what-if; Unit 15 GENERALIZES the CRN test to K candidates — every policy x conversion-grid candidate, within a seed-set, consumes the normals identical path-for-path across the survivor MFJ->single transition. Per-bucket draws are FORBIDDEN (they break CRN and re-open asset-location). The death-order conditional filter carries through unchanged: same seed, same draws, no re-draw.

items.claim: CONTRACT #6 — Recommend-second flow + the 10/10->surplus headline pivot (owned by Unit 16). The spine confidence answer is the FIRST beat (the magic moment, unchanged, never overwritten). The recommendation is the immediate SECOND beat — 'and here's what we'd do about it' — with comparative reasoning (why this beat the runner-up) ONE TAP DOWN (depth-on-demand, R4). The user tunes/overrides/re-picks the goal, both futures updating. It is CALM and INVITED, never a nagging alert/badge/engagement bait (R11). The 10/10 clamp pivot: when survival is a given (over-funded household / Tier-1 already maxed across futures), the headline honestly SWITCHES to the chosen surplus metric — 'you're safe either way; this keeps more from the IRS' — so the solver's signal is never eaten by the survival clamp. The active metric is always rendered explicitly so the user never silently re-bases between the spine beat and the recommendation beat.

items.claim: CONTRACT #7 — Hedge-on-headline lint + disclosed-omission rule (owned by Unit 16). Every recommendation grades its own confidence and the hedge rides the headline — depth-on-demand must never invert into certainty-on-top/caveats-hidden-below (R22). copyGuard's require-the-hedge lint (a positive/require assertion introduced in Act 3, NOT the legacy ban-list) is extended to assert the recommendation headline + grade copy each wear their probabilistic hedge by construction; certainty verbs stay banned (R12). All recommendation strings route through src/ui/copy.ts catalog (recommendation viz in src/viz stays string-free, receiving text as props — burned/063). Disclosed-omission rule: because a disclosed omission can INVERT a ranking (not just blunt a delta), ACA-PTC + IRMAA are already IN the model (Act 1); the remaining out-but-disclosed effects (NIIT, state tax) are disclosed in plain language ADJACENT to the delta, never silently dropped. One further effect is LEVER-SENSITIVE: when the chosen Tier-2 goal is 'leave more', a death-time §1014 basis step-up (taxable stepped up at death, inherited pre-tax fully taxable to heirs as IRD, Roth tax-free) MOVES WITH the sequencing/conversion lever and can invert which strategy leaves more after-tax. By the IN/OUT line's own falsifiable test (the lever moves which account is preserved into the estate AND the effect can invert the ranking) it belongs IN, not disclosed-and-omitted. So 'leave more' objective is the after-tax-to-heirs bequest (contract #4): a first-order §1014/IRD adjustment modeled into the bequest statistic, with the assumed heir tax bracket carried as a disclosed, R7-editable assumption surfaced adjacent to the leave-more delta. The lever-INERT NIIT + state tax remain the ONLY OUT-but-disclosed effects. The full-fidelity estate model (multiple heirs, state estate tax, trusts, precise IRD timing) stays chapter-two.

CONTRACT #8 — Spending is never solver-recommended (owned by Unit 15) + the stale-rec inversion (owned by Unit 17). (a) The solver's controls are ONLY the two funding levers — named drawdown policies x the conversion grid; the budget/spending shape is user-set input (floor essentials + discretionary surplus), never a control the solver moves. A tool must never recommend a LIFESTYLE; it shows honest consequences. (b) A saved recommendation is a real, executed action, so its staleness rule INVERTS the spine's Act-3 rule. The spine re-PRESENTS a saved verdict under its SAVED fixture vintage (so the number matches the screenshot) and only re-RUNS under current fixtures on demand. A recommendation cannot: a stale saved rec ALWAYS re-solves under CURRENT fixtures, and the staleness copy reads 'the action we recommended may no longer be advised,' NOT 'your number drifted.' Re-verifying the ACA legislative status is part of this (it can flip the whole pre-65 model and thus which strategy wins). A saved manual-control result (an Act-3 what-if, not an executed action) keeps the spine's re-present-under-saved-vintage rule; only a saved RECOMMENDATION inverts — the boundary the reset turns on (a saved control what-if ≠ a saved executed action).

Unit 14 — Solver validation harness (GATES Unit 15). Goal: make the recommendation's CORRECTNESS testable before the solver speaks — a hand-computable known-best oracle, K-candidate ranking-stability under CRN, calibrated confidence grades, and the held-out-seed defense against the optimizer's curse — so a confidently-wrong recommendation FAILS LOUD. Requirements: R22 (grade calibration), R25 (cardinal honesty bar), SC (recommendation half of two-tier correctness criterion).

Unit 14 Dependencies: Act 1's validated spine + CRN draw schedule, the tax-and-accounts overlay, the healthcare overlay (ACA fixed-point + IRMAA lag) the near-ties depend on, and src/engine/constants/ (the year-keyed table; the §Strand-5 + healthcare primaries PINNED is a hard prerequisite, contract #2). Has NO dependency on Unit 15 — it is built first by construction.

The candidate enumerator is SHARED, not duplicated: the policy x cliff-anchored-conversion-grid candidate generation (with the RMD-first legality filter) lives in src/engine/solver/candidates.ts, CREATED in Unit 14 (because rankingStability.ts must run the CRN check over the SAME candidate set Unit 15 later scores) and IMPORTED by both U14's harness and U15's search.ts — so 'built before any solver code' is honest and the two can never drift to different candidate sets.

Unit 14 Files to CREATE: src/engine/solver/candidates.ts (shared policy x cliff-anchored-grid candidate enumerator + RMD-first legality filter); src/engine/validation/optimalityOracle.ts (the known-best drawdown/conversion cases — the five cases i-v); src/engine/validation/rankingStability.ts (K-candidate CRN ranking check, run over candidates.ts); src/engine/validation/gradeCalibration.ts (robust-vs-fragile calibration + shrinkage calibration case + named-driver sensitivity probe); src/engine/validation/heldOutSeed.ts (seed-set A/B harness + deterministic B-family + ε-band measurement); src/engine/reference/solver-cases/ (COMMITTED, hand-derived oracle fixtures, NEVER generated, marked directional-until-pinned to §Strand-5/healthcare primaries — same discipline as Trinity/Bengen; EACH FIXTURE STORES ITS PRECONDITIONS — constant-rate; RMD/SS/cap-gains/cliff/bequest each on or off — and the harness refuses to apply a fixture's known-best outside its declared preconditions).

Unit 14 Files to MODIFY: src/engine/constants/ (the survival-equivalent ε constant is OUTPUT by this unit's calibration and stored here as an out-of-range-sentinel-guarded value); src/shared/model.ts (the second scenario seed seedB field — NET-NEW — alongside the spine's EXISTING seed: the field Act 2 already mints, now READ AS seedA, NOT a new field — so the spine headline still reproduces under 'the' seed; only seedB is added, under the Act-4 schemaVersion-3 bump — contract #2 / Unit 17). Tests: optimalityOracle.test.ts, rankingStability.test.ts, gradeCalibration.test.ts, heldOutSeed.test.ts.

items.claim: Unit 14 optimality oracle case (i): the conventional TAXABLE -> TAX-DEFERRED -> ROTH drawdown ordering is optimal ONLY in a constant-marginal-rate world — a flat rate, or income high enough that every year sits in one bracket, with NO RMD, NO SS taxation, NO cap-gains stacking, NO ACA/IRMAA cliff, and NO bequest motive — stated as the fixture's gating preconditions. A LOW-other-income world is explicitly NOT this case: it is the bracket-filling regime where (ii), not conventional ordering, is the hand-derived best — so the oracle must never be hardcoded to conventional ordering there.

Unit 14 optimality oracle case (ii): a BRACKET-FILLING Roth conversion optimum — fill to the top of a target bracket and no further — in a STRIPPED case where SS taxation, cap-gains/QD stacking, and ALL cliffs are OFF, so the in-bracket marginal rate is genuinely flat and 'bracket top' actually equals 'today's marginal = future marginal'. The REAL rule is marginal-rate equalization; 'bracket top' is a coincidence of the simplified world, never the rule the solver should learn.

Unit 14 optimality oracle case (iii): a CLIFF-AWARE case where filling past an ACA 400%-FPL ceiling or an IRMAA step LOSES, so the healthcare-blind ranking is sign-inverted (the tax-blind delta makes aggressive conversion look better than it is). Here the binding ceiling is the subsidy-aware MAGI/IRMAA-step line, NOT the bracket top — so (ii) and (iii) are SEPARATE WORLDS (healthcare off vs on) and a fixture's known-best is never applied across that boundary.

Unit 14 optimality oracle case (iv): a LEAVE-MORE AFTER-TAX case where the GROSS-bequest-best strategy is NOT the AFTER-TAX-best — the §1014 step-up/IRD treatment (contract #4/#7) inverts the ranking (e.g. preserving a taxable bucket that steps up at death beats converting a pre-tax bucket the heirs would owe IRD on at the assumed heir bracket) — so the oracle's known-best is the after-tax-to-heirs winner and a solver that argmaxes the gross bequest FAILS LOUD. This is the hand-derived guard that the after-tax objective is the one actually optimized.

Unit 14 optimality oracle case (v): a NO-CHANGE case where the conventional drawdown + zero conversion IS the known-best for the (model, goal): the oracle asserts the solver routes to the NO-CHANGE state (Unit 16) and does NOT crown a fabricated active move — which requires the search space to ALWAYS contain the conventional-order/conversion-0 candidate as a labeled baseline (Unit 15).

Unit 14: the oracle asserts the solver's RANKING puts the known-best candidate first; a PLANTED WRONG-BEST fixture must make the oracle FAIL LOUD (burned/070 — planted-fail self-test, the oracle must be able to fail).

Unit 14: Ranking-stability under CRN, generalized to K candidates (extends Act-3's 2-arm test). The RANKING — not just each pairwise delta — must be stable on the shared draw matrix. Assert all K policy x conversion-grid candidates, within one seed-set, consume the normals identical path-for-path across the survivor MFJ->single transition; perturbing only a candidate's conversion amount must not perturb any other candidate's draw consumption. PAIR EVERY CRN ABSENCE-ASSERTION WITH A PRESENCE COMPANION (burned/027): assert 'the harness ran N paths and at least one path crossed the survivor transition / an ACA cliff / an IRMAA step' so a vacuous zero-path pass cannot masquerade as stability.

Unit 14 grade calibration: the grades are ROBUST-across-futures ('just do it') vs FRAGILE ('coin-flip — here's what it hinges on'). Calibration asserts: a 'just do it' grade is emitted ONLY when the winner's lexicographic advantage over the runner-up holds on the held-out seed-set B with margin BEYOND the ε-band; 'coin-flip' when the held-out advantage falls WITHIN noise. The oracle hand-supplies one KNOWN-ROBUST case (a dominant strategy that wins on any futures) and one KNOWN-FRAGILE case (two near-tied strategies) and asserts the grade matches. The N=1 cold-read judges the grade's TONE; this oracle is the only judge of its CORRECTNESS (R25) — different gates, neither substitutes for the other.

Unit 14: because a SINGLE held-out B is unbiased but HIGH-VARIANCE, the grade is computed over a specified MINIMUM B PATH FLOOR (enough paths that the margin-vs-tolerance decision is not itself noise) and a GRADE-STABILITY CHECK asserts the grade for a fixed (model, goal) does not flip across independent held-out-B draws — a known-borderline case is forced to the conservative ('coin-flip') reading rather than allowed to luck-flip. The 'independent held-out-B draws' are a DETERMINISTIC B-FAMILY, not plural persisted seeds: the one persisted seedB indexes a fixed, well-separated SplitMix/hash family seedB[0..m-1] of m independent hold-out streams (m = the minimum-B-path-floor count), all RE-DERIVABLE from the single seedB — so the grade is both stability-checked AND byte-reproducible on re-entry (Unit 17 re-solves on the saved seedB and regenerates the identical family -> the identical grade). The per-solve compute profile (Unit 15) must budget the m-draw family, not one B.

items.claim: Unit 14: the grade also emits its 'what it hinges on' NAMED DRIVER (consumed by Unit 16, contract #7): gradeCalibration.ts runs a small SENSITIVITY PROBE — re-rank the top candidates under the ACA-enhanced-subsidy toggle and a fixture-vintage perturbation — and reports the single input whose flip moves the grade (e.g. 'depends on whether enhanced ACA subsidies return'); a pure seed-B near-tie with no identifiable input driver carries a sampling-noise-near-tie SENTINEL, never a fabricated input cause.

Unit 14: Grade vs display resolution reconciled — a graded-significant advantage that rounds BELOW one display tenth of the 'X of 10' headline must not render an UNCHANGED 'X of 10' under a 'just do it' (indistinguishable from no-change): the surface either shows the finer figure (surplus $ delta / a percentile-shift line) OR the grade requires the advantage to clear BOTH the seed-B ε-band AND one display tenth before 'just do it' (the sub-tenth win otherwise collapses into the no-change state).

Unit 14: Seed-set B and the grade thresholds are drawn under a FRESH-DRAW, USED-ONCE-PER-RELEASE, RE-DRAWN-ON-ANY-CHANGE-TO-CANDIDATES-OR-THRESHOLDS protocol; the N=1 cold-read may revise tone/copy but its feedback NEVER re-tunes the candidate set, thresholds, or the survival-equivalence tolerance against B-derived outputs (adaptive reuse silently re-optimisms B — the garden-of-forking-paths failure).

Unit 14 held-out-seed defense + ε-band measurement: heldOutSeed.ts runs candidate evaluation on seed-set A (selection) and seed-set B (reporting), each CRN-correct internally. SEED-SET B CARRIES THE DISPLAYED NUMBERS, NOT ONLY THE GRADE: the recommended figure and the no-action baseline Unit 16 renders both come from B (the seedA selection score is NEVER displayed — else the hero number is the curse-biased one). The K-candidate ranking-stability/CRN check runs on BOTH A and B. The survival-equivalent ε is CALIBRATED HERE against the optimality oracle (the constant is this unit's deliverable). Store ε with an OUT-OF-RANGE SENTINEL DEFAULT, never an in-range fallback (burned/062): an unset/uncalibrated ε must be DETECTABLY unset, never a plausible-looking 0.0x. The exact pinned ε value is DEFERRED to the §Strand-5/healthcare primary-pinning (contract #2) — directional-until-pinned because the directional fixtures decide the very near-ties it governs.

Unit 14: the ε resolves into TWO calibrated quantities (contract #2): a DISPLAY BAND measured on B (the rendered interval) and a SELECTION TIE-TOLERANCE keyed to the variance of the pairwise DIFFERENCE under CRN (a pre-specified/theoretical SE, or computed A-side) that ALONE decides survival-equivalence — the latter is NEVER a B-measured level band reused to rank. BOTH are sentinel-guarded.

Unit 14 mints the OPAQUE 'oracle-cleared' TOKEN (contract #1) — constructable ONLY by this harness on a clean pass — that Unit 15's solve-as-recommendation entry point takes as a REQUIRED PARAMETER (so a recommendation that skips validation is a COMPILE error). The token is withheld until EVERY check passes on the pinned fixtures: the optimality oracle (all FIVE cases, including the no-change and after-tax-leave-more guards), K-candidate ranking-stability, grade calibration (with named-driver probe + deterministic B-family), the held-out-seed defense, AND the structural pinning clause — every rec-relevant §Strand-5 + healthcare primary pinned (directionalUntilPinned === false) and ε calibrated (a still-directional rec-relevant constant or an uncalibrated-ε sentinel withholds the token). This mirrors Act 1's no-unkeyed-write structural seam.

Unit 14 patterns to follow: Act 1 seeding/CRN + the externally-derived-golden discipline; burned/070 (planted-fail self-test — the oracle must be able to fail); burned/027 (absence-tests need presence companions); burned/062 (no in-range default fallbacks — the ε sentinel); the 'Solver validation' strand of docs/research/engine-validation-and-tax.md.

Unit 14 PICK-QUALITY defense is IN scope, not deferred. An honest grade alone does NOT make a stochastic near-tie PICK optimal — a 'coin-flip'-graded recommendation can still crown a seed-A-overfit winner over an equally-good or better candidate. So Unit 15's select.ts applies SELECTION-STAGE SKEPTICAL/BAYESIAN SHRINKAGE of the seed-A candidate scores TOWARD THE CONVENTIONAL-ORDERING PRIOR before the argmax, and Unit 14 carries the CALIBRATION CASE that proves it — a planted near-tie between two NON-CONVENTIONAL candidates must default to the conventional (shrunk) pick UNLESS a candidate's advantage survives the shrinkage, and a known-dominant strategy must survive it unchanged. This closes the gap a no-change-vs-conventional safety net alone leaves: the curse bites hardest among two AGGRESSIVE near-tied candidates, neither near the conventional baseline.

Unit 14 Execution note: test-first and FIRST IN THE ACT — the oracle + ranking-stability + calibration fixtures are authored and passing BEFORE any src/engine/solver/ code exists. This is the literal expression of 'validation gates the solver.'

Unit 15 — Solver core. Goal: search the bounded strategy space (named drawdown policies x a conversion grid) on identical CRN futures, score each candidate on the lexicographic objective whose metric IS the headline metric, select a byte-identical winner + retained runner-up, within the on-demand compute budget (or trigger the WASM promotion) — RANKING candidates, never RE-IMPLEMENTING decumulation. Requirements: R9 (a strategy over two coupled controls), R21 (lexicographic objective; objective ≡ headline metric), R23 (retain the runner-up), R24 (healthcare couples into the objective). GATED by Unit 14 (contract #1).

Unit 15 Dependencies: Unit 14 (the validation gate); Act 1 (the spine + per-year update function + CRN draw schedule + the sequencing POLICY substrate; the tax-and-accounts overlay; the healthcare overlay — ACA fixed-point, IRMAA 2-yr lag, HSA bucket, the two MAGI calculators); Act 3 (the budget — essentials = Tier-1 floor, discretionary = Tier-2 surplus; the manual-control roth.ts per-year update shape); Act 2 (memoryModel — the solver run is dispatched through the same orchestrator + request-epoch as the spine).

Unit 15 Files to CREATE: src/engine/solver/search.ts (the policy x conversion-grid cross-product evaluator on identical CRN draws — REUSES the spine's per-year update function, does not re-implement decumulation); src/engine/solver/objective.ts (the lexicographic Tier-1/Tier-2 score); src/engine/solver/select.ts (deterministic byte-identical selection + retained runner-up — contract #3); src/engine/solver/cancel.ts (request-epoch cooperative cancellation); src/engine/solver/profile.ts (the WASM measurement harness — the compute-profile gate). Tests: search.test.ts, objective.test.ts, select.test.ts, cancel.test.ts, profile.test.ts.

Unit 15 Files to MODIFY: src/shared/model.ts (the CHOSEN-GOAL field — the Tier-2 pick — under the Act-4 schemaVersion-3 bump; the saved-recommendation record is Unit 17's); src/store/memoryModel.ts (dispatch the on-demand solve + carry its request-epoch, extending the Act-2 worker handle); src/engine/engine.worker.ts (expose the solve entry behind the Unit-14 oracle-cleared gate).

items.claim: Unit 15 search space is BOUNDED and NAMED (R-locked, docs/product.md §4 D4): named drawdown policies {proportional, taxable-first, pre-tax-first, bracket-fill} (the Act-1 sequencing substrate) x a conversion grid {amount x years}. The solver evaluates the CROSS-PRODUCT of candidates; the grid resolution (amount step, max years) is a bounded set — exact resolution DEFERRED to implementation. This is NOT a continuous optimizer (a full continuous optimizer + a 'die-with-zero' solver + SS-claiming-age are explicitly chapter-two, deferred).

Unit 15: the grid is CLIFF-ANCHORED, not uniform — a CORRECTNESS requirement, not a resolution-tuning knob. The ACA 400%-FPL cliff and the IRMAA steps are discontinuities whose optimum sits exactly at the just-under-threshold dollar, so each candidate year includes grid points PINNED JUST UNDER EVERY ACTIVE ACA/IRMAA THRESHOLD plus a LOCAL BISECTION REFINEMENT around them; a uniform grid generically steps over that point and can neither find the just-under-cliff optimum nor avoid recommending a cliff-tripping amount. Relatedly, bracket-fill fills to the BINDING EFFECTIVE CEILING for the year — the subsidy-aware MAGI line in ACA years, the next IRMAA step post-65, a marginal-rate-aware bracket edge otherwise — NEVER the nominal tax-bracket top (which overshoots the cliff the instant healthcare is on). The candidate generation is the shared candidates.ts (authored in Unit 14).

Unit 15: the 'no-action baseline' is a LABELED, SCORED candidate — the user's CURRENT strategy, not a notional default (contract #6 anchor). Every Unit-16 comparison (no-change decision, rendered delta, tax-aware reframe) is 'current strategy -> recommended,' so the baseline must be a real candidate scored on the IDENTICAL seed-A and seed-B draws as every other. The search FORCES the user's current configured strategy into the candidate set as a labeled baseline: their current sequencing policy + current conversion, defaulting to proportional/conversion-0 if none is set. A returning Act-3 user who set a CUSTOM per-bucket drawdown order (not one of the four named policies) is handled explicitly — that custom order is evaluated as its own labeled baseline point OUTSIDE the named-policy x grid cross-product (scored on the same draws), so the delta is never silently anchored against the conventional default the user does not actually hold. The conventional-order/conversion-0 candidate is ALSO always present (Unit-14 no-change oracle case (v) and the shrinkage prior both require it).

Unit 15 RANKS, does not re-decumulate (the solver-on-top principle). Each candidate is evaluated by running the EXISTING spine + overlays through the SAME per-year update function the manual controls drive (Act-3's roth.ts shape) with that candidate's policy + conversion event — so order-of-operations can never drift between the spine, the manual controls, and the solver. The reduce-to-spine golden invariant is INHERITED, not re-proven: with conversion = 0 and the conventional drawdown, a candidate's distribution is byte-identical (same seed) to the validated Trinity/Bengen spine — the golden cases are never perturbed by the solver layer (docs/architecture.md §5).

Unit 15 deterministic byte-identical selection (contract #3), with pick-quality shrinkage: select.ts FIRST applies a deterministic skeptical/Bayesian SHRINKAGE of the seed-A candidate scores toward the conventional-ordering prior (the Unit-14-calibrated lever for PICK quality, not just grade honesty) — a candidate only displaces the conventional pick if its advantage SURVIVES the shrinkage; a known-dominant strategy survives it unchanged. Selection then = quantized lexicographic objective over the SHRUNK scores + a fixed lexicographic tie-break (policy enum order -> conversion amount -> years) + a seeded sub-stream ORTHOGONAL to seed-sets A/B (used only for a residual deterministic tie-break, never for simulation). The winner + the RETAINED RUNNER-UP (R23 — the runner-up is kept, not discarded, so Unit 16 can show 'why this beat it') are reproducible from (model, seedA, seedB, goal) alone. No clock/entropy/Math.random.

Unit 15 the 10/10-clamp/surplus regime (feeds contract #6): when Tier-1 is maxed across futures (survival a given), the objective's active discriminator is Tier-2 — the solver emits the surplus winner and flags the regime so Unit 16 can pivot the headline. The clamp is on the DISPLAY of Tier-1; the SELECTION still uses the raw pre-clamp Tier-1 to decide survival-equivalence (mirroring Act-3's raw-pre-clamp monotonicity rule). The surplus-regime flag requires A and B to AGREE within an over-funded ε — and 'over-funded' is an ε-TOLERANCE, not an exact 10/10: the flag trips when the B-rendered Tier-1 is within the display-band ε of the ceiling, so a genuinely over-funded household whose B happens to miss one path by a rounding step is not permanently denied the pivot. Both disagreement directions pinned: (a) Tier-1 maxed on A but a real survival gap on B (beyond over-funded ε) -> the flag does NOT trip (no false 'safe either way' the displayed B number would contradict); (b) B safe-either-way but the winner was SELECTED on A's Tier-1 discriminator (candidates not Tier-1-equivalent on A) -> the flag does NOT trip either, because pivoting while the pick was made on a survival edge would diverge objective from headline (contract #4). The pivot fires ONLY when both A and B agree the floor is non-binding.

Unit 15: Spending is never a control (contract #8a). The budget + spending shape (go-go-years front-loading vs level) are READ-ONLY input to every candidate; the solver moves only sequencing + conversion. No candidate alters a budget line.

Unit 15 candidate-legality filter before scoring (validate-before-mutate, burned/021). Before a {policy, amount, years} candidate is scored, each year is checked for legality: past RMD age the year's RMD is a FORCED ordinary-income floor TAKEN FIRST and is NON-CONVERTIBLE, so the conversion is CLAMPED to the pre-tax balance remaining AFTER the RMD, and a grid amount that exceeds post-RMD convertible headroom (or that would convert in lieu of the RMD) is REJECTED AS INFEASIBLE (an out-of-range sentinel, never silently scored). The search-space generation owns this — Act 1 enforces the RMD when RUNNING a candidate, but an infeasible candidate must never reach scoring in the first place.

Unit 15: per-account buckets are a HARD PRECONDITION of the recommendation (the budget-only-path guard). The solver searches sequencing x conversion, which require per-person pre-tax/Roth/taxable/HSA buckets — the second beat CANNOT be emitted without them. Buckets always arrive from the account-level intake (Act 2 / R35), so the absent-buckets case is a DEFENSIVE EDGE — a legacy v1 vault or a direct path. The recommendation-invite TRIGGERS the RothAccounts mini-intake when buckets are absent (reusing the Act-3 component), and the solver NEVER runs on a defaulted bucket split (burned/062: a defaulted split is a silent measurement, the calm-but-wrong shape).

items.claim: Unit 15: a chosen Tier-2 goal is an equally hard precondition (the no-discriminator guard). The lexicographic objective needs a Tier-2 goal to break survival-equivalent ties, so the solve is NEVER dispatched while goal === unset-sentinel, mirroring the bucket guard. The second beat presents the GoalPicker FIRST (Unit 16) — 'what matters most to you above safety?' — and only dispatches the solve once a goal is set; it never runs a Tier-1-only solve and crowns the deterministic tie-break (policy enum order) as if it were advice. This also closes the over-funded-with-no-goal case: for a Tier-1-maxed household an unset goal would leave the solver with no discriminator and nothing to pivot the headline to, so the surplus pivot is likewise unreachable until a goal exists.

Unit 15 solve-once-on-demand + cooperative cancellation (request-epoch). The interaction is SOLVE-ONCE-ON-DEMAND, not live-drag: a recommendation is computed when invited (the second beat) or re-invited (a goal re-pick/tune). cancel.ts extends the Act-2 request-epoch + Act-3 generation-counter discipline to the SOLVE: each solve carries the epoch it was dispatched for and cooperatively cancels if a newer request supersedes it (checked between candidates / between seed-sets), so a fast goal re-pick never commits a stale recommendation. The solve has an explicit CALM PENDING STATE: while a solve runs, the second-beat surface shows a quiet 'working on it…' state, the prior recommendation (if any) is held VISIBLY-STALE-BUT-LABELED rather than blanked, and NO partial or fabricated recommendation paints before the solve commits; the committed result replaces pending atomically (notify-once). A multi-second solve on a mid-tier phone must read as 'the tool is working,' never 'the tool broke' — the pending copy is an Act-4 cold-read subject.

Unit 15 the WASM measurement gate (the decided trigger, the port deferred). profile.ts measures the real on-demand solve cost: named-policies x conversion-grid x 1k paths x (SS fixed-point + ACA fixed-point + IRMAA lag), across BOTH seed-sets A and B, on a MID-TIER PHONE. If the on-demand solve EXCEEDS the budget, WASM moves from fast-follow to LOAD-BEARING — the trigger is MEASURED, not guessed; the WASM port itself is DEFERRED (the TS baseline ships, the measurement decides the promotion; see WASM CSP landmine in docs/architecture.md §9-§10). The budget threshold value + the mid-tier reference device are DEFERRED to implementation (instrument first, per eye-in-loop discipline). select-on-A + grade-on-B roughly DOUBLES the per-candidate evaluation vs a single-seed solve — the profile must measure both, not extrapolate from one.

Unit 15: the profile must run a deliberately COMPUTE-WORST-CASE scenario — longest horizon, largest cliff-anchored grid (the most active ACA/IRMAA thresholds -> most pinned points + bisection refinements), BOTH the pre-65 ACA and post-65 IRMAA regimes exercised — not a median one, or the WASM promotion is decided on a cost a real near-cliff, long-horizon, large-pre-tax household will blow past (the SS/ACA fixed-points converge in 2-3 bounded passes, so the worst case is driven by HORIZON + CLIFF-COUNT/GRID-SIZE, not iteration depth). The profile budgets BOTH seed-sets AND the m-draw held-out B-family (Unit 14), not a single B.

Unit 15: a BOUNDED IN-MVP FALLBACK LADDER exists that does NOT depend on the deferred WASM port (since both solver axes ship co-equal, the worst case is real): (a) a COARSE-THEN-REFINE two-stage search — a cheap coarse grid prunes the field, and the cliff-anchored just-under-threshold points + bisection are spent ONLY around the surviving candidates (cliff anchoring stays a correctness requirement but applied to survivors, not the full cross-product, so the un-cuttable points don't multiply across every coarse candidate); (b) a stated CANDIDATE-COUNT CEILING for the interactive solve; (c) if the measured budget is still blown AND WASM is not yet built, the recommendation DEGRADES HONESTLY rather than blocking — the calm pending state with cooperative-cancel runs the full-fidelity solve, or a reduced interactive-path solve is shown explicitly labeled with a 'full-precision' confirm — it never silently down-samples below the path floor the held-out grade needs. The MVP SHIPS (degraded-but-honest), it does NOT block on the WASM port.

items.claim: Unit 15 the K-candidate solve-result WIRE-SHAPE (extends Act 1's worker transfer contract). Act 1 pins the single-run worker result (typed-array buffers via Comlink.transfer, detached on the worker side, fresh per run — docs/architecture.md §11); the solve returns K candidates, so the wire shape is made explicit: the solve returns ONE structured payload carrying the FULL seed-B distributions for the figures Unit 16 renders — the WINNER, the RETAINED RUNNER-UP, and the NO-ACTION BASELINE — plus the grade + named-driver + surplus-regime flag, with ONLY those distributions' buffers in the transfer-list; the pruned/losing candidates return SCALAR lexicographic scores only (structured-clone, no buffers), never their full distributions. The per-solve allocation is sized for this bounded set (THREE distributions + scalars), not K full distributions — keeping Act 1's 'fresh per run, retains none' discipline at K-candidate scale.

Unit 15 patterns to follow: Act 1 CRN + the reduce-to-spine invariant; Act-3 roth.ts (reuse the per-year update function, never re-implement decumulation; raw-pre-clamp selection); the Act-2 request-epoch / Act-3 generation counters for cooperative cancellation (burned/005); burned/062 (no in-range default — the goal field has an explicit 'unset' sentinel, never a silent default goal); burned/021 (validate-before-mutate — the candidate-legality/RMD-first filter); the §Strand 4/5 + healthcare research.

Unit 16 — Recommendation surface. Goal: surface the solver's output as the calm SECOND beat — a confidence-graded recommendation that never contradicts the spine, with the hedge on the headline, the runner-up retained and the comparison one tap down, the modeled omissions disclosed adjacent to the delta, every input + reasoning visible/editable, and an honest 10/10->surplus pivot — landing as EARNED, never overconfident. Requirements: R10, R4, R11, R12, R13, R14, R7, R21, R22, R23, R24.

Unit 16 Dependencies: Unit 15 (solver output — winner, grade, retained runner-up, surplus-regime flag); Act 2 (the spine confidence statement the second beat follows + the copyGuard catalog + the outcome-state set; the colorblind-safe viz primitives + the 'X of 10' display contract — built under the project's back-nine-design law: color is never the only signal); Act 3 (the budget two-tier essentials/lifestyle reading; the require-the-hedge lint + the manual-control surfaces the goal re-pick reuses; the sharpen loop the recommendation inputs become editable through).

Unit 16 Files to CREATE: src/ui/Recommendation.tsx (the second-beat surface); src/ui/ConfidenceGrade.tsx ('just do it' vs 'coin-flip — here's what it hinges on'); src/ui/RunnerUp.tsx (the retained runner-up + 'why this beat it'); src/ui/GoalPicker.tsx (the Tier-2 pick — leave more / pay less tax / live bigger now); src/viz/RecommendationViz.tsx (the recommended-vs-current two-series, STRING-FREE — text via props from copy.ts, reusing Act-2's encoding tokens). Files to MODIFY: src/ui/copy.ts (recommendation strings + grade copy + omission-disclosure copy); src/ui/copyGuard.ts (recommendation slot allowlist + extended require-the-hedge assertion); src/store/memoryModel.ts (hold the chosen goal + the un-saved recommendation hypothetical). Tests: recommendation.test.tsx, confidenceGrade.test.tsx, runnerUp.test.tsx, goalPicker.test.tsx.

Unit 16 recommend-second, never recommend-first (contract #6; R10). The invited affordance is a REAL, NAMED control (its existence and shape decided here, exact pixels/copy a cold-read deliverable): a single calm affordance rendered just below the spine confidence statement that the user activates to open the second beat — NEVER an auto-trigger on scroll/load (violates R11's 'invited') and NEVER a directive 'Get our recommendation' CTA (violates R12's banned certainty/imperative voice). Activating it opens the GoalPicker as the FIRST interaction (goal precedes the solve, Unit 15), so the second beat BEGINS with 'what matters most to you above safety?' rather than a fabricated ranked answer.

Unit 16 the NO-CHANGE recommendation state (R25 — the recommender's calm-but-wrong shape). When the winner is WITHIN the A-side selection tolerance of the no-action baseline — the conventional order is FREQUENTLY already optimal (literally Unit-14 oracle case (i)/(v)) — the second beat does NOT manufacture an active move: it renders a NO-CHANGE state (reusing Act-2's outcome-state vocabulary) — 'you're already on the best path we found; here's the close runner-up if you're curious' — wearing its hedge, the runner-up still one tap down. No-change is a SELECTION decision (it picks WHAT to recommend), so it is decided on the CRN-difference SELECTION tolerance computed at selection (contract #2), NEVER on a seed-B level band — using B to decide no-change-vs-active re-contaminates the held-out; seed-B then supplies only the displayed numbers and the grade for the no-change verdict. The no-change state CARRIES ITS OWN CALIBRATED GRADE (Unit 14) and its headline WEARS THE HEDGE by construction (require-the-hedge covers the no-change copy). Fabricating an active recommendation when no change beats the status quo is the recommender's cardinal-sin shape. Precedence with the surplus pivot: when the surplus regime is active AND the winner is within the selection tolerance of the baseline on Tier-2, the two states COMPOSE — render 'you're safe either way, and you're already on the best surplus path we found', NEVER the active 'keeps ~$X more' surplus claim (which would fabricate a surplus gain that does not exist).

items.claim: Unit 16 confidence grading on the headline (contract #7; R22). The grade ('just do it' / 'coin-flip — here's what it hinges on') rides the HEADLINE, never buried in tapped-away math. The grade is the CALIBRATED grade from Unit 14's held-out-seed reporting — the surface RENDERS it, it does NOT recompute robustness. The 'coin-flip' render names WHAT IT HINGES ON (the near-tie's sensitive input — e.g. 'this depends on whether the enhanced ACA subsidies return'). The 'what it hinges on' line requires a SENSITIVE-INPUT ATTRIBUTION distinct from the seed-B margin grade — a seed-B dispersion cannot name WHICH input a ranking hinges on, and a legislative/scenario sensitivity (the ACA-enhanced toggle) is invisible to it — so Unit 14's gradeCalibration sensitivity probe EMITS the named driver (re-ranking the top candidates under the ACA-enhanced toggle + a fixture-vintage perturbation, reporting the single input whose flip moves the grade) alongside the grade; the surface only renders it, and a pure seed-B near-tie carries the sampling-noise-near-tie sentinel — a sampling-framed hinge, never a fabricated input cause.

Unit 16 objective ≡ headline, rendered explicitly (contract #4). The recommendation's headline metric IS the metric the solver optimized — rendered in the spine's 'X of 10' voice ('this pushes the survivor's essentials from 7 of 10 to 9 of 10') so it can never contradict the spine answer. EVERY displayed figure — the recommended-strategy figure, the no-action baseline it is compared against, AND the retained runner-up's figure — is rendered from the held-out seed-set B (contract #2): the shown shift is therefore unbiased (never the seedA SELECTION score, the optimizer's-curse-inflated figure the whole Unit-14 machinery exists to defeat) and internally CRN-consistent (every number on the one seedB draw matrix -> both the recommended-vs-baseline and the recommended-vs-runner-up deltas are pure strategy signal, not an A-vs-B sampling artifact). The seedA score SELECTS the winner (and retains the runner-up) only; it is NEVER rendered — for either the winner or the runner-up. The 10/10->surplus pivot (contract #6; R21): when Unit 15 flags the surplus regime (survival a given), the headline honestly SWITCHES to the chosen surplus metric — 'you're safe either way; this keeps ~$X more from the IRS / funds ~N more years of travel' — with the active metric NAMED so the user never silently re-bases between beats. The pivot reuses the spine's over-funded outcome-state vocabulary.

Unit 16 tax-blind->tax-aware reframe, inherited from Act 3 (contract #6; R8/R10). The Act-2 spine headline (the first beat) runs the tax + healthcare overlays OFF — it is TAX-BLIND, on seedA — and is NEVER overwritten (Act-1 seed/headline identity). The recommendation's baseline + recommended numbers are the TAX-AWARE picture (overlays ON, on seedB), so the no-action baseline can legitimately read DIFFERENT FROM the tax-blind spine number the user anchored on. Inherit Act-3's DELTA-LED reframe — 'now that we know your account types, this is the tax-aware picture' — so the shift reads as a SHARPENING to a truer picture, NEVER a silent downgrade of the magic-moment number; the active baseline is NAMED so the differentiation 'move' (the delta — both numbers tax-aware, both on seedB) reads against a consistent anchor, not against the tax-blind spine figure. The magnitude the copy attributes to taxes is ONLY the seedB overlays-off->on delta (the strategy/tax signal on one draw matrix); the baseline-vs-spine difference is framed QUALITATIVELY as 'a sharper picture now that account types are known,' NEVER quantified as a tax-caused drop — the residual seedA<->seedB difference is SAMPLING, not taxes, and is never shown as a number the user could misread as a downgrade.
