items.claim: Unit 16 comparative transparency, runner-up retained (R23). RunnerUp.tsx keeps and surfaces the runner-up (Unit 15 retained it) — 'why this beat the runner-up,' not a formula dump. Rendered via RecommendationViz as a two-series recommended-vs-runner-up (or recommended-vs-current) using Act-2's colorblind-safe encoding tokens + the delta-as-hero treatment (Act-3's TwoFutures lineage); the N=1 reader is color blind, so the delta carries a NON-COLOR hero signal (the project's back-nine-design law — color is never the only signal).

Unit 16 disclosed omissions adjacent to the delta (contract #7; R24). ACA-PTC + IRMAA are already IN the model (Act 1) because a disclosed omission can INVERT a ranking. The remaining OUT-but-disclosed effects — NIIT, state tax — are disclosed in plain language NEXT TO the delta, never silently dropped; when the chosen goal is 'leave more', the bequest is the AFTER-TAX-TO-HEIRS figure (a first-order §1014/IRD adjustment modeled INTO the objective — never the gross figure), and the ASSUMED HEIR TAX BRACKET is the disclosed, R7-editable assumption surfaced adjacent to the leave-more delta; a conversion that trips an ACA cliff or an IRMAA step is SHOWN, not silently optimized over. The held-fixed SS CLAIM AGE is disclosed adjacent to the delta — it is NOT a solver-optimized control in MVP (chapter-two), yet changing it would move provisional-income taxation / ACA-MAGI / IRMAA-MAGI and could invert the ranking, so a calm note ('this assumes your current claim ages') rides the delta. For 'live bigger now'/'leave more' goals, the delta funds the user's CURRENT chosen spending shape (a user-set input, contract #8a) — a one-line honesty note says the recommendation optimizes the FUNDING of the shape you set, it does not endorse or propose a lifestyle. When a recommended strategy's delta leans on the ACA effect, the SLCSP-benchmark-level and CSR caveats (Act 3 — the SLCSP is the user-input the entire ACA fixed-point keys on) are surfaced adjacent to the rec delta too (at least by reference to the Act-3 healthcare surface), so an ACA-affected recommendation is never presented more certain than its inputs — especially when a FALLBACK (non-real) SLCSP is in use.

Unit 16 every input + reasoning visible/editable; the user stays pilot (R7, R10d). R7 gains weight under recommend-second: the recommendation exposes its inputs AND its reasoning for the user to trust and approve. The user tunes/overrides/re-picks the goal via GoalPicker (reusing the Act-3 sharpen loop + manual-control surfaces); on a re-pick, the solve re-runs (Unit 15, request-epoch) and BOTH futures update. A GoalPicker with no goal yet selected uses an EXPLICIT UNSET SENTINEL (burned/062), never a silent default goal.

Unit 16: saving a recommendation is an EXPLICIT COMMITTED gesture, never inferred (the bridge to Unit 17's 'executed action'). A solved recommendation lives in memoryModel as an UN-SAVED HYPOTHETICAL (Unit 15) until the user DELIBERATELY commits it — an explicit, calm 'save this recommendation' gesture (pixels deferred to cold-read; its existence decided here). The tool NEVER auto-saves on solve, on close, or on a goal re-pick — because Unit 17 treats a saved recommendation as a REAL, EXECUTED ACTION with serious staleness consequences ('the action we recommended may no longer be advised'), and that severity is only honest if the user consciously committed. The un-saved hypothetical can be tuned, re-picked, abandoned freely with no staleness obligation; only the explicit commit mints the saved-recommendation record (Unit 17's schemaVersion-3 write).

Unit 16 the require-the-hedge lint extended to the recommendation (contract #7; R12). All recommendation strings route through the copy.ts catalog; RecommendationViz (in src/viz) stays STRING-FREE, receiving text as props (burned/063). copyGuard's require-the-hedge lint (the positive/require assertion from Act 3) is extended to assert the RECOMMENDATION HEADLINE + the GRADE COPY each carry a probabilistic hedge; certainty verbs ('guaranteed / optimal / locks in / you will save') stay banned. The 'just do it' COLLISION is resolved explicitly: require-the-hedge applies to the rendered grade SENTENCE/COPY (which must wear its hedge — e.g. 'across the futures we tested, this holds up — just do it'), and EXEMPTS the bare fixed enum label ('just do it' / 'coin-flip') as an internal identifier — so the punchy robust label survives while the user-visible grade copy still hedges by construction. NEW recommendation slots added to the allowlist: the recommended-strategy descriptor (policy name + conversion amount/years as user-echo, not a product claim), the grade label, the ~$X surplus delta, and the X of 10 shift — added to the catalog-enumeration test so they pass by construction.

Unit 16 the optional honest-limits note (R13). The 'this is a model — validate big, irreversible moves with a pro' note is available adjacent to the recommendation on HONESTY grounds (not a Terms requirement) — calm and invited, not a nagging gate; it lives OUTSIDE the require-the-hedge input the same way the static disclaimer is surface-scoped.

Unit 16 patterns to follow: Act-2 copyGuard + the outcome-state set + the X of 10 display contract; Act-3 TwoFutures delta-as-hero + the props-from-copy.ts string-free viz rule; Act-3 require-the-hedge lint; emil-design-eng (calm second-beat entrance, NO count-up on the surplus dollar); compound-engineering:frontend-design (the recommendation reads as a calm co-pilot, not a dashboard); back-nine-design (project design law — color is never the only signal).

Unit 16 exit condition: passing the N=1 cold-read on the recommendation — EARNED (not overconfident), the 'coin-flip' grade HONEST (not wishy-washy or alarming), the comparison reading as TRANSPARENCY (not a bait-and-switch) — is an Act-4 exit condition (R25; the cold-read judges TONE, Unit 14 judges CORRECTNESS). Also: a recommendation must VISIBLY MOVE the spine answer ('6 of 10 -> 8 of 10') AND be correctly confidence-graded (the differentiation success criterion).

Unit 17 — Stale saved-recommendation handling. Goal: treat a saved recommendation as the real, executed action it is — on re-entry, RE-SOLVE it under current fixtures (never re-present a stale strategy as still-advised), say 'the action we recommended may no longer be advised' (not 'your number drifted'), and re-verify the ACA legislative status that can flip the whole pre-65 model. Requirements: R7, R10, R24 (ACA legislative volatility re-verified), R25.

Unit 17 Dependencies: Unit 15 (the re-solve path); Unit 16 (the re-presented recommendation surface + grade render); Act 3 (the per-surface staleness map + the returning-user re-entry this INVERTS for a recommendation); Act 1 (the encrypted store + the saved-recommendation record's persistence — docs/architecture.md §7.3); src/engine/constants/ (the year-keyed fixtures whose vintage drives staleness).

Unit 17 Files to CREATE: src/store/recStaleness.ts (the INVERTED recommendation-staleness rule + the ACA-status re-verify gate). Files to MODIFY: src/shared/model.ts (the SAVED-RECOMMENDATION RECORD — the recommended strategy + its as-recommended fixture-vintage stamps + a SOLVER/ENGINE-CODE VERSION STAMP + seedA/seedB/goal — under the single Act-4 schemaVersion-3 bump; the 'never-depleted' surplus / serialization sentinels decided here, NOT Infinity/NaN — archive/do-not-disturb/009. Execution status is NOT tracked — the sentinel denotes a non-depleting surplus value, never an execution state; the inversion below is precautionary, not a claim the action was taken); src/store/staleness.ts (Act 3 — register the recommendation as a surface whose staleness rule INVERTS); src/ui/ReEntry.tsx (Act 3 — surface the re-solved recommendation + the 'may no longer be advised' copy). Tests: recStaleness.test.ts, reentry-recommendation.test.tsx.

Unit 17 the staleness rule INVERTS for a recommendation (contract #8b). Act-3's spine rule: RE-PRESENT a saved verdict under its SAVED fixture vintage (so the number matches the screenshot), and only RE-RUN under current fixtures on demand. A recommendation CANNOT do that — it is a real action a user may execute with real dollars — so the rule inverts: a stale saved recommendation ALWAYS re-solves under CURRENT fixtures before it is shown, and is NEVER re-presented under its saved vintage as if still advised. The saved record's as-recommended vintage is kept FOR PROVENANCE + STALENESS DETECTION, never for re-presentation-as-current.

Unit 17 the staleness copy reads as an ACTION WARNING, not a number drift. When the saved recommendation's fixture vintage (tax-table / RMD-age rule / senior-bonus sunset / ACA-PTC regime / IRMAA brackets) has moved since save, the copy reads 'the action we recommended may no longer be advised' and the re-solved current recommendation is shown alongside — NOT 'your number drifted' (true for the spine verdict but dangerously wrong for an action). The QUIETEST stale shape is the SAME strategy whose outcome DEGRADED — the re-solve returns the same recommended strategy but its grade fell from 'just do it' to 'coin-flip,' or its delta turned NEGATIVE (the once-helpful action now hurts) under current law. That reads 'still fine' to a user who recognizes their familiar strategy, so it carries its OWN copy distinct from both 'may no longer be advised' and silent re-presentation — 'this is still the best of the options, but it's now a coin-flip / no longer ahead — here's what changed,' surfacing the degraded grade or sign flip prominently.

Unit 17 a recommendation is stale when ANY rec-relevant fixture moves. The recommendation depends on more fixtures than the spine verdict (the spine is tax-blind): a saved rec is flagged stale when the TAX-TABLE vintage, the RMD-AGE rule, the SENIOR-BONUS-DEDUCTION sunset, the ACA-PTC legislative regime, OR the IRMAA brackets have moved (findings §Strand 5 + healthcare). Each routes through the canonical src/engine/constants/ vintage stamps — no fixture vintage is re-typed here. A saved rec is ALSO stale on MODEL-INPUT DRIFT, not only fixture drift: a confirmed per-bucket BALANCE/SPLIT change (a conversion sized to a specific pre-tax pool is far more balance-sensitive than the tax-blind spine — a drifted pool can trip an ACA cliff or make the saved amount infeasible) AND a BUDGET-WINDOW ADVANCE (a time-boxed line past its endYear) both flag it — reusing Act-3's existing per-bucket balance-drift confirm, not a new mechanism. And because the selected number is reproducible from (model, seedA, seedB, goal) ONLY given fixed solver code, a SOLVER/ENGINE-CODE VERSION CHANGE is itself a staleness trigger (grid resolution, ε, objective quantization, or tie-break order all move the winner/grade for identical fixtures): it forces a re-solve and surfaces the delta as a recommendation change, never hidden behind byte-identity.

Unit 17 re-verify the ACA legislative status — it can flip the whole model (contract #8b; R24; healthcare §2). The enhanced-ACA-subsidy status is LIVE, possibly-retroactive policy; if the enhanced regime is restored (possibly retroactively), the 400% FPL cliff DISAPPEARS and the pre-65 conversion calculus FLIPS — which can INVERT which strategy wins. recStaleness.ts carries the ACA-status as a first-class staleness driver: a saved recommendation computed under the 2026 cliff-on base case is ALWAYS flagged for re-solve if the legislative status has changed since save. (The build-time re-verify of the legislative status itself is a roadmap validation gate, verify:aca; this unit CONSUMES its result.) Distinguish a FORWARD regime change (re-solve forward) from a RETROACTIVE one: the enhanced regime could be restored possibly retroactively to 2026 (healthcare §2), so a past action's cost can change after the fact — which forward-re-solve does not address. For the retroactive case surface a distinct, generic note — 'a recent law change may apply to a past year, so an action you may already have taken could now carry a different cost — worth revisiting with a pro' — phrased generically because execution and tax-year are not tracked.

As-built ACA legislative status: the recommendation base case is the 2026 CLIFF-ON case (the enhanced-ACA-subsidy 400% FPL cliff is currently in effect). The enhanced regime is LIVE, possibly-retroactive policy — could be restored possibly retroactively to 2026, which would make the 400% FPL cliff disappear and flip the pre-65 conversion calculus. Re-verified every build via verify:aca.

Unit 17 GATE-RED-AT-RE-ENTRY fallback (the undefined-state guard). The re-solve calls Unit 15, which refuses to emit a recommendation while the oracle-cleared token is absent (contract #1). The token is withheld for MORE THAN ONE REASON, and the fallback BRANCHES ON WHY rather than always blaming the law: (a) the ACA legislative status is UNVERIFIED (re-verified every build, so it can be unverified exactly when the law is in flux — the case this unit most cares about) -> 'we can no longer stand behind this and cannot currently re-verify the law — do not act on it until the status is confirmed'; (b) a rec-relevant primary is still DIRECTIONAL or ε is uncalibrated (the pre-launch/un-pinned-build state, which contract #2 makes the DEFAULT until pinning completes) -> 'this recommendation isn't validated on this version yet — don't act on it until it is'. In every case NEITHER path is legal — the inversion forbids re-presenting the stale rec as advised, and the gate forbids a re-solve — so the saved strategy is shown CLEARLY MARKED with the matching reason, never re-presented as still-advised and never silently suppressed. (recStaleness.ts reads the token's withheld-reason; it does NOT assume the law is the cause.)

Unit 17 the saved-recommendation record's 'never-depleted' surplus / serialization sentinels (archive/do-not-disturb/009 [DND 009]). Decide the saved record's sentinel shape BEFORE the schema locks: a recommendation the user saved but a field like 'expected surplus = never depleted' must serialize WITHOUT Infinity/NaN silently becoming null through JSON.stringify/IndexedDB. Use an explicit OUT-OF-RANGE SENTINEL, the same discipline the spine model uses (docs/architecture.md §7.3 / §8). Execution status is not tracked — the sentinel is a surplus value, not an execution flag.

Unit 17 the v2->v3 vault upgrade — its trigger, and the first-save-mints-v3 path (inherits Act-1 atomicity). The v3 bump fires on EXACTLY ONE EVENT: the first EXPLICIT SAVE of a recommendation (Unit 16's deliberate commit gesture) — never on a goal-pick, never on a solve, never on an un-saved hypothetical (so seedB is always derived and the goal always set before a v3 record exists; a v3 blob with a null seedB is unreachable). Persisting the saved-recommendation record + seedB/goal is the first v3 disk write; on an EXISTING on-disk vault it goes through Act-1's MODEL-ONLY RE-ENCRYPT (same DK, fresh IV, wraps untouched) — the same atomic path Act 3 uses for v1->v2 — so an ABORTED v2->v3 upgrade still decrypts the intact v2 (a half-written vault is the same catastrophic class as Act-1's first-save-atomicity landmine). A brand-new user whose first-ever Save IS a saved recommendation (intake -> budget -> recommendation-invite -> buckets -> goal -> commit, with no prior v1/v2 on disk) mints a v3 blob DIRECTLY through Act-1's keyed first-save path — the first Save writes whatever schemaVersion the in-memory shape implies (v1, v2, or v3); the model-only re-encrypt UPGRADE path is only for an existing on-disk vault advancing versions, never a precondition for reaching v3.

items.claim: Unit 17 re-solve reuses the saved seeds for continuity, current fixtures for honesty. The re-solve runs Unit 15 on the SAVED seedA/seedB/goal (so the futures are continuous with what the user saw — not a fresh random scenario) but under the CURRENT fixtures AND the current confirmed balances/budget (so the strategy is current) — never the saved PRE-CONFIRM balances; a drifted per-bucket split re-confirms through Act-3's gate BEFORE the re-solve. Reusing the saved seedB under changed fixtures does NOT contaminate the held-out, even when the candidate set's size/shape changes (a moved grid resolution, RMD age, or feasibility): the hold-out's validity comes from seedB ⊥ seedA (the seed-input decorrelation, contract #2), NOT from any binding to a particular candidate set — seedB is an independent SCENARIO set, not a per-candidate object, so a winner selected on A and graded on the saved seedB-family over the CURRENT candidates is unbiased regardless of how the candidate set changed. The one invariant: the re-solve RECOMPUTES the grade on the seedB-family over the CURRENT candidates (never re-presents the saved grade), and it still SELECTS ON A, GRADES ON B — never selecting on B. (Resolution of the apparent 'stale seedB vector' concern: continuity-of-futures = same seeds; hold-out validity = B ⊥ A; the two do not conflict.)

Unit 17 patterns to follow: Act-3 staleness map + re-entry (invert the spine rule for the recommendation surface); archive/do-not-disturb/009 (JSON-persisted sentinels — decide before the schema locks); burned/062 (no in-range default for the saved-goal/vintage fields); findings §Strand 5 + healthcare §2 (the ACA legislative landmine).

Unit 17 exit condition: a stale strategy silently presented as current is the cardinal sin extended across time (R25); this unit is the structural guard against it. Passing the N=1 cold-read on Unit 17's staleness copy is an Act-4 exit condition (cold-read judges TONE, Unit 14 judges CORRECTNESS): the 'may no longer be advised' copy (honest, not alarmist), the same-strategy-degraded case (a familiar strategy whose grade fell or delta turned negative must read as honest recalibration, never 'still fine / no change'), the retroactive-ACA past-cost note (informational, not catastrophizing), and the gate-red reasons (each honest about why, never blaming the law when a primary is merely un-pinned) are each first-class subjects.

Unit 17 Execution note: test-first on the INVERSION (a moved fixture must re-solve, never re-present) and the SENTINEL ROUND-TRIP (decide the saved-record serialization before the schema locks) — both are correctness anchors, not UI polish.

STANDING as-built fact carried in the changelog: per-account buckets, contributions, and healthcare inputs arrive UP-FRONT from the account-level intake (the 2026-06-08 accumulation fold, master R26-R39, the account-level R35 setup), so the first answer is account-aware from the start and the overlays are active wherever the entered streams support them. Consequently U15's absent-buckets case is a DEFENSIVE EDGE (legacy v1 vault or direct path), and U16's reframe story re-derives from the account-aware baseline at build time. The three honesty rules STAND UNCHANGED: the delta-led honesty rule, the never-overwrite-the-saved-headline rule, and the never-quantify-the-seedA<->seedB-residual rule. Everything else in this act (oracle-before-solver, held-out seed-B machinery, objective ≡ headline, U17's inverted stale-rec rule) stood unchanged through the fold.

inventories.label: feat-social-security
inventories.oneLineRole: The as-built record of the Social Security benefit sub-engine — PIA-driven own benefit, Method C spousal excess, and §202 survivor (RIB-LIM) — documenting every SSA rule, factor, fixture, citation, decision, and the survivor-floor bug it shipped with.

items.claim: The Social Security sub-engine is SHIPPED, reviewed (the /ultramode-code-review holistic integration pass), and pinned. Coded 2026-06-14, code-reviewed 2026-06-14. It computes each person's actual annual SS benefit (own reduction/credit, Method C spousal excess, §202 survivor with RIB-LIM) from a per-person PIA + claim age inside a new PURE sub-engine src/engine/socialSecurityBenefit.ts that feeds the existing cash seam.
items.duplicatedIn: docs/roadmap.md (You-Are-Here unit status); project memory project-the-back-nine.md
items.fossilNote: Lives in features/ as a feature doc keyed to when SS was added; the as-built status belongs in the roadmap's per-unit status, the rules/decisions belong in architecture/product.

items.claim: The sub-engine is NOT a new engine. It is a pure (household PIAs, claim ages, birth years) → per-person annual benefit streams function, computed PRE-LOOP, that populates the existing PersonOffsets.socialSecurityReal slot. cashTermsForYear, maxBenefit, the §86 provisional-income tax overlay, and the fuck-off-date sweep are all downstream and structurally unchanged.

The old model asked the user to do the actuarial math: every person handed the engine a flat already-claim-adjusted annual benefit (socialSecurityReal); the survivor took the larger single benefit once they reached their OWN claim age — $0 before. Three correctness gaps a recommender-grade tool cannot tolerate (honesty bar RISES for a recommender): (1) spousal underivable by a layperson; (2) max(own,spousal) is calm-but-wrong; (3) the survivor stub was conservative-but-coarse.

Gap 1: Spousal was underivable by a layperson — a user cannot read their spousal benefit off ssa.gov because it is a function of the OTHER spouse's PIA; asking for it guaranteed a wrong or blank input. This was the ATC decision that opened the unit: compute spousal automatically.

Gap 2: SSA does NOT pay the larger of own-vs-spousal when claimed early — it pays the gently-reduced own benefit IN FULL plus a separately-reduced spousal EXCESS (POMS 'Method C', RS 00615.020). The two pieces reduce on DIFFERENT schedules, so the true total EXCEEDS max(). Verified divergence: own PIA $1,000 / spouse PIA $3,000, both claim at 62 → true $1,025/mo vs naive-max $975/mo, a $600/yr understatement that scales with own-PIA and how early a dual earner claims. Shipping max() would systematically under-credit exactly the dual-earner households this tool serves.
items.duplicatedIn: §4, §11 (divergence fixture), verified SSA rule-set table (Method C row)

items.claim: Gap 3: The survivor stub ('$0 until own claim age') was one-signed safe (never optimistic) but zeroed out 1–5+ years of a substantial survivor benefit when a spouse dies while the survivor is 60–65 — the high-stress scenario a retirement co-pilot must get right.

Per the 2026-06-14 ATC ruling, survivor §202 is folded in — the correct survivor COMPUTATION, not the P4 claim OPTIMIZER — because the old $0-until-own-claim survivor stub materially shortchanged early widowhood.

Requirements/decision trace: ATC #1 (2026-06-14) — compute spousal AUTOMATICALLY, input becomes PIA + claim age per person. ATC #1 + POMS RS 00615.020 — spousal is Method C EXCESS not max() (supersedes the stated rule). ATC #2 boundary (2026-06-14) — survivor §202 computation folded in, survivor optimizer deferred to P4. ATC (stop-early honesty) — intake routes user to the mySSA $0-future-earnings figure. Engine contract — sub-engine is PURE, pre-loop, PIA=0 ⇒ byte-identical to prior socialSecurityReal=0 spine. Constants discipline (burned/057,061,063; DND 012) — new statutory Sourced table, goldens from POMS printed examples never engine-derived.

IN SCOPE (the correct computation): own-benefit early reduction (pre-FRA) + delayed credits (post-FRA), exact integer fractions; the Method C spousal excess (two reduction schedules, the worker-must-be-entitled temporal gate, the excess floor); deemed-filing collapse to ONE claim-age decision per person (both cohorts post-1954); survivor §202 — age-reduced survivor benefit (71.5% @60 → 100% @ survivor-FRA), the deceased's DRC flow-through, and the RIB-LIM cap.

items.claim: DEFERRED to P4 (recommend-second engine), explicitly NOT here: (a) the survivor two-stage claim OPTIMIZER — survivors are exempt from deemed filing so an optimal widow(er) chooses when to switch between survivor-first→own-at-70 and own-first→survivor-later; the engine optimizes NO claim ages yet so it would be a lever with nothing to pull it; this unit ships a defensible fixed claim-timing default (§6). (b) The accumulation-state PIA recompute / year-of-death AIME recomputation (RS 00615.320 'fictitious life PIA') — second-order, the entered PIA is carried as the real figure (a named, bounded simplification). (c) Divorced-spouse / child-in-care / DIB benefit branches — out of the married-couple front door (the worker-must-have-filed prerequisite must NOT be generalized to a divorced spouse if ever added — POMS GN 00204.035). (d) The family-maximum (150–188% of PIA) — rarely binds for a childless 2-person couple; named, not modeled.

items.claim: The cash seam: cashTermsForYear (src/engine/simulate.ts) sums o.socialSecurityReal per claimed-alive person and the survivor takes maxBenefit. The sub-engine DOES NOT touch this function — it changes only what dollar lands in PersonOffsets.socialSecurityReal and adds the time-dependent excess/survivor streams.

The offset build: offsets + maxBenefit are computed once pre-loop, a pure function of entered inputs. The sub-engine slots in HERE, pre-loop, so it consumes ZERO draws and is CRN-invariant across date-search candidates (the fuck-off-date sweep shifts a claim OFFSET, never a claim AGE).

The tax overlay: taxableSocialSecurity (src/engine/taxOverlay.ts, IRS §86 / Pub 915 Wksht 1) consumes the benefit DOLLAR and is agnostic to its derivation. Computing the benefit upstream is seamless to the provisional-income layer — no double-count risk, the overlay never re-derives the benefit.
The input model: PersonInputs (src/shared/model.ts) carries pia + socialSecurityClaimAge; PersonInputsV3 extends PersonInputs, so ScenarioV3 transitively persists the field this unit swapped.

Migration blast radius: 84 occurrences of socialSecurityReal/socialSecurityClaimAge across 16 files (heaviest: simulate.test.ts ×28, questions.tsx ×12, intakeMap.test.ts ×5, sanity.ts ×5, scenarioCodec.test.ts ×4). This was a SEMANTIC migration not a rename: the old value was the already-adjusted benefit, the new pia is the FRA benefit. Every fixture/test with a non-FRA claim age had to be reinterpreted (a flat $X claimed at 62 was $X; now PIA $X claimed at 62 becomes $0.70·X). Two simulate.test.ts fixtures hand-reimplemented the seam and asserted byte-exactness so they were REWRITES not value-reinterprets. The adversarial verify stage refuted a false '74-occurrences' count — 84 stands.

§1 input swap: PersonInputs DROPS socialSecurityReal (the already-adjusted benefit) and GAINS pia (the real, today's-dollar benefit-at-FRA off the statement). socialSecurityClaimAge STAYS (now consumed by the sub-engine instead of being a passive label). Both per-person. A non-working / no-record person enters pia: 0 (the reduce-to-spine zero).

§1 PIA entry period (ratified): ask MONTHLY (the figure the statement shows), STORE ANNUAL (×12), validate the ceiling in monthly terms at the field — mirrors the existing spendEntryPeriod discipline. Validation (intake/sanity.ts): the PIA ceiling is a NET-NEW sanity rule (new rule id + CopyKey + test — there is no antecedent money-sanity rule on the SS field; only ss-claim-window exists). The claim-age ∈ [62, 70] bound ALREADY EXISTS (SS_CLAIM_MIN/SS_CLAIM_MAX, sanity.ts) — a re-confirm, the deemed-filing single-decision window.

§2 — A new canonical constants module src/engine/constants/socialSecurity.ts: one year-keyed module, every figure a Sourced<T> with directionalUntilPinned: false (the verify sweep IS the pin) and legalBasis set (these are STATUTORY — 42 U.S.C. §402, 20 CFR 404, the POMS section — stable, not annually re-indexed like tax brackets).

§2 shapes (new interfaces in constants/types.ts): FullRetirementAge — birth-year → MONTHS (804 for 1960+; graduated 1955–59 band; the Jan-1 prior-year rule encoded in the lookup, not the caller). ReductionSchedule — { firstMonths: 36, firstRatePerMonth, beyondRatePerMonth } stored as INTEGER FRACTIONS (5/9, 5/12, 25/36, 2/3 of 1% — i.e. 1/180, 1/240, 1/144, 1/150) so 62/FRA67 falls out as exactly 168/240 = 0.7000. Three instances: WORKER_REDUCTION, SPOUSE_REDUCTION, DRC (the credit side; monthsCap is derived per person = 840 − fraMonths — 36 at FRA 67, 46 at FRA 66y2m — never a literal 36, which would contradict this table's graduated-FRA provisioning).

§2 SURVIVOR_REDUCTION — keyed to span exactly 28.5% from age 60 to survivor-FRA (compute the per-month fraction from the span; do NOT hardcode 19/40), + the DWB flat-28.5% floor. RIB_LIM — { floorPctOfDeathPia: 0.825 } (the 'larger-of' logic lives in code; the constant is the floor). SPOUSAL_RATE = 0.50; DEEMED_FILING_DOB_CUTOFF = 1954-01-02.

§2 SPOUSAL_RATE carries reVerifyEveryBuild-class monitoring (like the ACA entry): a scored-but-unenacted proposal to phase 50%→33% by 2042 was found; the constant must catch enactment at build time, not drift silently.

§3 adjustOwnBenefit(pia, claimAgeMonths, fraMonths): n = fraMonths − claimAgeMonths (whole months early; negative ⇒ delayed). Early (n>0): factor = n ≤ 36 ? (180−n)/180 : (192−(n−36))/240. Delayed (n<0): factor = 1 + min(−n, drcMonthsCap)·(2/3)/100, where drcMonthsCap = 840 − fraMonths (the FRA→70 span — 36 at FRA 67, 46 at FRA 66y2m; a literal 36 under-credits a delayed claim on a mixed-cohort household, e.g. a 1958-born spouse of a 1969-born). At FRA (n=0): factor = 1. benefit = floorToDime(pia · factor) — dime-round DOWN, the final step, on the dollar. A golden asserts factor = 0.7000 (pre-round) at 62/FRA67 and 1.24 at 70/FRA67.

§4 Method C excess for person L on H's record (H = higher PIA = argmax(pia)): excessFull = max(0, SPOUSAL_RATE·H.pia − L.pia); ownAdjusted = adjustOwnBenefit(L.pia, L.claim, L.fra) [worker schedule 5/9…]; excessAdj = reduceSpouseExcess(excessFull, L.claim, L.fra) [spouse schedule 25/36…, NO DRCs]; L.benefit = ownAdjusted + excessAdj. reduceSpouseExcess: with n = L.fra − L.claim (months early), factor = n ≤ 36 ? (144−n)/144 : (180−(n−36))/240 (25/36 first-36 then 5/12 beyond) — at 62/FRA67 exactly 156/240 = 0.65. Numerator constants differ from worker formula (144/180 here vs 180/192 in §3) because the first-36 reduction differs (25% vs 20%). Two SEPARATE reduction schedules off the SAME claim-month-count. Excess floored at 0 (when L.pia ≥ 50%·H.pia it degrades to own-only). Spousal base is H.pia UNREDUCED — never H's adjusted benefit, never DRC-inflated. NO DRCs on the excess (flat past FRA). Each household has at most one spousal direction (lower-PIA spouse on the higher's record).

items.claim: §5 Deemed filing: both cohorts (born 1969/1972, turn 62 in 2031/2034) are post-1954 → fully subject. A single claimAge per person drives BOTH their own benefit and their spousal excess (no separate spousal claim age, no restricted application). A test asserts no path produces a spousal claim age ≠ the own claim age (outside the unmodeled child-in-care/DIB exceptions). The SURVIVOR branch is the lone exception and retains independent timing (§6).

§6 Survivor §202: when the first death occurs, the survivor's SS each year = max(ownStream, survivorStream) — and this max() is a LEGITIMATE larger-of (survivor vs own are ALTERNATIVE entitlements; collect the higher), UNLIKE the §4 spousal max() that was wrong (spousal is ADDITIVE own+excess). survivorBenefitFull = the deceased's ADJUSTED benefit (including the deceased's DRCs — flow-through per RS 00615.301/.702), the DRC-correct analog of the old maxBenefit. RIB-LIM: if the deceased had claimed reduced RIB before death, cap survivorBenefitFull at max(0.825·deceasedPIA, deceasedActualReducedBenefit).

items.claim: §6 Age reduction — LOCK-FLAT (cardinal-rule-load-bearing): the survivor stream starts at max(survivor age 60, first-death year); its reduction factor is LOCKED at the survivor's age at that start offset and held FLAT for the rest of the horizon. It does NOT ramp upward toward 100% as the survivor ages. The '71.5% @60 → 100% @ survivor-FRA' schedule is over the CLAIM AGE (a survivor who claims later gets a higher factor) — NOT a post-claim age-ramp. A per-year ramp would optimistically overstate guaranteed income on exactly the early-widowhood paths this unit exists to fix — the calm-but-wrong sin. (survivor-FRA = 67 here, keyed separately.)

items.claim: §6 Ratified claim-timing default (ATC-confirmed 2026-06-14): the survivor claims the survivor benefit AS SOON AS ELIGIBLE (max(60, death)), locks the reduced factor, and receives max(own, survivor) each year. The adversarial review confirmed this is one-signed conservative ONLY under the lock-flat reading: it closes the early-widowhood gap (ATC intent) while leaving the survivor's optimal two-stage upside (survivor-first → own-at-70, the deemed-filing-exempt lever) ON THE TABLE for P4's optimizer — never an optimistic assumption baked in here. The replaced $0-until-own-claim stub is gone; reduce-to-spine still holds (no death ⇒ this code never runs ⇒ byte-identical).

§7 The engine seam: the orchestrator householdBenefitStreams(people) runs ONCE PRE-LOOP (alongside offsets/maxBenefit) and is the entry point for everything. Three components wired differently by time-shape: (1) Own benefit → a resolved per-person SCALAR: adjustOwnBenefit(L.pia,L.claim,L.fra) is a single claim-age-locked dollar that DIRECTLY REPLACES the old PersonOffsets.socialSecurityReal scalar; PersonOffsets stays scalar; the ~10 PersonOffsets literals and cashTermsForYear's signature are a VALUE REINTERPRET not a shape change. (2) Spousal excess → a time-gated per-person term: $0 until max(L.claimOffset, H.claimOffset) (the worker-must-be-entitled START gate, RS 00202.001) AND returns to $0 at H's death offset (the END gate — the excess terminates at the worker's death and is replaced by the survivor benefit; omitting it DOUBLE-COUNTS guaranteed income on death paths); mirrors contributionsForYear's per-path death-truncation shape. (3) Survivor benefit → a per-PATH selection (the real new plumbing).

items.claim: §7 Survivor benefit per-PATH selection plumbing: the old cashTermsForYear kept only a boolean survivorClaimed + scalar maxBenefit — it discarded WHICH spouse died and carried no age. §6 needs all three: (a) the deceased's INDEX (recover it — previously thrown away), (b) the survivor's AGE at t (people[i].currentAge + t), (c) the deceased's RIB-LIM-capped survivor base — so precompute TWO survivorBenefitFull values (one per possible decedent) pre-loop and SELECT per path at the death offset. The survivor branch is rewritten to the §6 max(ownStream, survivorStream).

§7 CRN invariant (corrected mechanism): the date-search (dateSearch.ts) varies ONLY retirementAge; currentAge, socialSecurityClaimAge, pia, and birthYear are held VERBATIM — so every claim OFFSET (claimAge − currentAge) is INVARIANT across candidates (the sweep shifts the retire offset, not the claim offset). Own, the gated excess, and the survivor selection are therefore all candidate-invariant — computed once, ZERO draws. (The accumulation-state PIA recompute is deferred to P4, so moving retirementAge cannot perturb a PIA either.)

The 84-site audit budgeted accordingly — simulate.test.ts was the heavy lift.

The unit shipped in two reviewed passes: a pure-core review (insight 039 locked the pure survivorBenefitAnnual contract) and a holistic integration review of the wiring commit. Three guards are load-bearing for the cardinal rule; one of them was a BUG the integration review found, not a plan item.

items.claim: realizedClaimAgeAtDeath — the survivor-floor optimistic-overstatement bug (insight 040). The plan's §7 said to build the deceased's survivor base from d.socialSecurityClaimAge (the household's PLANNED claim age). The post-wiring holistic review found this was an OPTIMISTIC OVERSTATEMENT of the survivor floor — the cardinal sin — on exactly the early-widowhood paths the §202 unit exists to harden. THE BUG: on any Monte-Carlo path where the death offset preceded the claim offset, the deceased NEVER LIVED TO FILE, yet the seam credited the full delayed-retirement credit of a claim they never made: a plan-70 breadwinner dying at 68 got a 1.24× PIA survivor base instead of the 1.08× they actually earned; dying at 66 (before FRA) got 1.24× instead of the full PIA. Reachable, not measure-zero — the longevity sampler's minimum death age is 66 and claim-70 is the de facto household default, so deaths at 66–69 before a planned-70 claim are a common path class.

Why the pure core wasn't wrong: survivorBenefitAnnual correctly trusts deceased.claimAge as the REALIZED claim age — that is its input contract, locked by insight 039. The bug lived entirely in the INTEGRATION SEAM, the only layer that knows the stochastic timeline (which path, which death year); it fed the pure core a PLANNED value as if it were realized.

The fix (shipped): realizedClaimAgeAtDeath(plannedClaimAge, birthYear, ageAtDeath) = max(min(planned, ageAtDeath), ⌊FRA⌋). Called in the seam to realize the deceased's claim age before constructing the BenefitPerson. Capping at age-at-death strips the unearned credits; the FRA floor keeps an unfiled PRE-FRA death from picking up a spurious early-claim reduction (it lands on the full PIA — 20 CFR §404.313, POMS RS 00615.301/.690). EXACT for a whole-year FRA (both shipped cohorts = 67); for a fractional-FRA cohort it floors to ⌊FRA⌋, a sub-one-year CONSERVATIVE (never optimistic) residual. The pure core is untouched. Six hand-derived goldens (DND/012) pin it: the realization at each boundary, the integration dollar ($19,587.60 vs the buggy $22,490.40), the nonzero-excess START/END gates, and the own-wins selection.

The coverage gap that hid the bug: every fixture reaching the survivor branch used an already-claimed deceased (negative claim offset ⇒ death always after filing), so the death-before-claim path was structurally untested — an adversary's mutation that stripped the START gate and leaked the excess into the survivor branch survived 915/915 tests. Two sibling gaps rode alongside: no fixture drove a NONZERO spousal excess through cashTermsForYear (the START/END gates were untested), and the survivor max(ownStream, survivorStream) was tested only survivor-wins (survivor pia=0), never own-wins. All three are now covered.

The lasting lesson (insight 040): a pure unit's input contract assumes its inputs are already realized; realizing a PLANNED input that a stochastic process can preempt is the SEAM's job, never the pure core's. A discriminating test must drive the PREEMPTION, not just the plan-equals-outcome case. See docs/insights/040-an-integration-seam-must-realize-a-planned-input-the-stochastic-timeline-can-preempt.md.

As-built file map: src/engine/constants/socialSecurity.ts (canonical statutory constants table, §2); src/engine/constants/types.ts (FullRetirementAge, ReductionSchedule, RIB_LIM shapes, §2); src/engine/socialSecurityBenefit.ts (pure sub-engine: adjustOwnBenefit, reduceSpouseExcess, householdBenefitStreams, survivorBenefitAnnual, realizedClaimAgeAtDeath); src/engine/simulate.ts (the seam: pre-loop householdBenefitStreams wiring, own-scalar reinterpret, per-year excess term, per-path survivor selection, realizedClaimAgeAtDeath realization, §7); src/engine/taxOverlay.ts (taxableSocialSecurity §86, unchanged §8); src/shared/model.ts (PersonInputs.pia + frozen PersonInputsLegacy for v1/v2 codec arms); src/intake/questions.tsx, copy.ts, intakeMap.ts, sanity.ts (D1 PIA question + stop-early routing + PIA-ceiling sanity rule, §9); src/engine/__tests__/socialSecurityBenefit.test.ts (POMS golden oracles, §11); src/engine/__tests__/socialSecurityBenefit.pbt.test.ts (property tests, §12).

Resolved open question — Monthly vs annual benefit granularity: RESOLVED annual. The engine is annual-real; the DRC 'January-after-the-year-earned' lag (RS 00615.690 §B) and the dime-rounding are MONTHLY rules. At annual granularity the lag is a self-correcting sub-12-month slice at the only anchor that matters (age 70, where it's zero). Documented as an intentional abstraction in the constants comment.

Sub-engine type contracts named: BenefitPerson (constructed in the seam, consumed by survivorBenefitAnnual); the per-person 'streams' are own (scalar), the spousal excess (time-gated term), and the survivor (per-path selection). H = argmax(pia) is the higher earner; L is the potential spousal recipient on H's record.

inventories.label: feat-other-income
inventories.oneLineRole: The build-ready feature plan for R40 (other ongoing non-earned income in retirement — pension/rental/alimony/annuity/other): the requirements trace, per-type defaults, scope boundaries, the nine load-bearing KTDs, the five engine seams, the five implementation units, risks, provenance corrections, and verified tax facts.

items.claim: R40 is PLANNED, build-ready, ZERO code. Nothing is built yet; the lifecycle block is intentionally empty. Grounded against HEAD dc674dff by a 4-agent code-grounding pass, then hardened by three review passes. This plan amends docs/product.md §7 with R40.

items.fossilNote: Lives in features/ as a feature plan; the requirements entry it describes lives in product.md §7. The status-banner narration of WHEN/HOW it was reviewed is fossil; the as-built PLANNED status is the survivor.

items.claim: The engine today models exactly TWO income concepts: earnedIncomeReal (which STOPS at retirement) and Social Security. It has NO concept of ongoing non-earned income (pension/rental/annuity/alimony that keeps paying after work stops). R40 adds a generic per-person income stream.
items.duplicatedIn: docs/product.md (R40 entry, supersedes 'two income streams' premise)

items.claim: R40 adds a generic per-person income stream, entered opt-in off the 5-minute path, compiled in intakeMap to pre-deflated real-$ gross + taxable vectors (in two death-state variants — KTD-4), integrated at the cash-netting (seam 1) and ordinary-income (seam 2) seams (SS-§86 / ACA-MAGI / IRMAA-MAGI ride through), with survivor continuation realized at the owner's sampled death in the path loop.

Test-drivers (Briggsy's friends): one with rental income; one whose wife draws a teacher's pension. The pension is the single most dangerous number in the app — whether it survives her death (and at what %) and whether it keeps up with inflation is the whole widow's picture. Getting either wrong is exactly the calm-but-wrong-optimistic sin. v1 either rounds conservative OR discloses its direction for every simplification.

R40 is NEW scope — zero mention of pension/rental/other-income in the locked R1–R39 requirements. It fits the north-star (honest answer for a real couple, NOT a FIRE calculator): these are real income streams a household already receives, not early-retirement engineering. The identity bound keeps it there.
items.sourceSection: Why this amends the locked contract

items.claim: The cardinal-rule constraint on R40: the taxable portion of a stream has to move EVERY income/MAGI site consistently and atomically (SS taxation, ACA subsidies, IRMAA tiers all key off MAGI). Every survivor/COLA/basis simplification must either round conservative OR be disclosed with its direction named — an opt-in optimistic simplification that isn't disclosed is still the sin.
R40.1 — Model a generic per-person ongoing income stream with type ∈ {pension, rental, alimony, annuity, other}; the type seeds defaults only.

R40.2 — Each stream carries: gross annualRealToday, startAge, optional endAge, a COLA mode ∈ {real-flat, nominal-flat, fixed-pct} (+ colaPct), a taxableFraction ∈ [0,1] (default 1), and a survivorPct ∈ [0,1].
R40.3 — Compile each stream to pre-deflated real-$ per-year vectors; the engine is a dumb consumer; survivor-% is pre-applied as a second variant at compile time (KTD-4).

R40.4 — The taxable portion enters ordinary income such that SS-§86 provisional, ACA-MAGI, and IRMAA-MAGI all move consistently in one atomic change, including the already-receiving × working-year IRMAA reconciliation (KTD-9).
R40.5 — Survivor continuation is realized at the owner's sampled death in the path loop, selecting the pre-weighted survivor variant, locked at the death offset, never ramped (KTD-4).
R40.6 — Reduce-to-spine byte-identity: a household with no streams is byte-identical (same seed) to the current Trinity/Bengen spine.

R40.7 — Intake is opt-in off the 5-minute guided path; the no-safe-default fields surface on the guided path regardless of the collapsed advanced tier: the survivor-% prompt for any continuing stream (pension/annuity/rental/other — alimony is survivorPct = 0 by law) and the alimony post-2018 agreement-date.
R40.8 — Ship the 'other' catch-all stream alongside the four named types. R40.9 — Add an R40 requirements entry amending the locked R1–R39 contract.

R40.10 — All correctness goldens are externally derived (DND/012); intake/restore validation is finiteness-first then range; engine-consumed figures obey the constants discipline; user-facing display-hint figures live in referenceData.ts, NEVER @engine/constants.

Per-type defaults table. PENSION: COLA default nominal-flat, fully taxable, survivor=prompt (no safe default, MUST-ASK = survivor % / QJSA election). RENTAL: real-flat, fully taxable, survivor ~100%, none forced. ALIMONY: nominal-flat, taxable derived from agreement date, survivor 0% (terminates at death), MUST-ASK = agreement executed before/after 12/31/2018. ANNUITY: nominal-flat, fully taxable (qualified) / exclusion-ratio (non-qual), survivor=prompt, MUST-ASK = qualified vs non-qualified. OTHER: nominal-flat, fully taxable, survivor=prompt. The type label SEEDS these; intake surfaces them for confirm.

The alimony agreement date is the highest-leverage field in the whole feature (verified): an instrument executed AFTER 2018-12-31 (or a pre-2019 one expressly modified to adopt TCJA) is NOT taxable to recipient and invisible to MAGI; an instrument ON/BEFORE 2018-12-31 IS taxable and DOES lift MAGI. Never default it. A pre-2019 agreement merely modified after 2018 stays taxable UNLESS the modification expressly adopts the new rules — so ask 'did the modification expressly adopt the post-2018 tax rules?', default = no.

Identity bound: R40 is NOT a FIRE lever and NOT a general income ledger. A new type must clear 'a real driver receives it and the answer depends on it' or it doesn't ship — the 'other' catch-all inherits that fence; dividends/1099/crypto are OUT unless a driver has one.
No live price/market fetch — CSP connect-src 'self' forbids it; everything is user-entered (docs/architecture.md §10).

Survivor-specific term/end gate is OUT (v1 forward landmine). KTD-4's two-variant linear pre-weighting holds BECAUSE v1 streams share one end gate across both variants. A stream whose survivor benefit has a different term than the owner benefit (period-certain J&S, survivor terminating on remarriage) would break the elementwise survivor = Σ streams·survivorPct relation.

DEFERRED — Rental sale events (depreciation recapture §1250 25%, cap-gains-on-sale, step-up-at-death): OUT — ongoing income only. Direction: slightly OPTIMISTIC (ignores depreciation shield eroding → real taxable rent rises; ignores recapture tax on future sale); disclosed.

items.claim: DEFERRED — Net-rental real-rise → OPTIMISTIC and it COMPOUNDS at the ACA cliff (disclosed with MAGNITUDE). Gross rent tracks inflation but the fixed-nominal depreciation shield erodes, so taxable net rent rises in real terms. v1 holds net rent REAL-FLAT and models rental taxableFraction = 1 (conservative on fraction, but flat trajectory understates late-horizon MAGI). The danger is NOT a smooth slope error: the omitted real-rent-rise is exactly the dollars that push a pre-65 household OVER the 400% FPL subsidy cliff (a discontinuity), where the miss is the ENTIRE unsubsidized premium for the bridge years. v1 discloses THIS MAGNITUDE in rental copy (not 'slightly optimistic') + a Unit 3 cliff-compound fixture; the upgrade (model a modest real-rise; needs BLS rent-CAGR figure verified first) is noted, not built.
items.duplicatedIn: Risks table; Provenance corrections (BLS rent-CAGR); Unit 3 test scenarios

items.claim: DEFERRED — Annuity/pension basis-recovery dynamics → OPTIMISTIC, opt-in, disclosed. The true exclusion-ratio / Simplified-Method tax-free portion is a FIXED NOMINAL $ that shrinks in real terms then STOPS when basis is recovered (then 100% taxable). v1 uses a CONSTANT taxableFraction, modeling the exclusion as NEVER exhausting → understates late-life MAGI → optimistic. The fully-taxable DEFAULT is conservative; an opt-in user who enters an exclusion fraction accepts an optimistic simplification — disclosed in copy.

DEFERRED — Alimony payer-death termination → OPTIMISTIC, disclosed (Briggsy decided: disclose for v1). Alimony ends at recipient's death (survivorPct=0 at owner=recipient's death) AND at the payer's death — but the payer has no presence/sampled death in the household model. v1 pays alimony for the recipient's full modeled life, overstating safety if the payer dies first. Disclosed, not modeled.

DEFERRED — Compounding-only COLA → the optimistic side of the fork, disclosed. Simple (non-compounding) COLA erodes faster in real terms; v1 models COMPOUNDING (the common case, but the optimistic side). fixed-pct COLA compounding convention is golden-pinned; simple-COLA deferred.
DEFERRED (OUT, disclosed) — NIIT (3.8% above $250k MFJ MAGI); state-level alimony decoupling; annuity LIFO for non-annuitized partial withdrawals (v1 models annuitized streams).

items.claim: KTD-1 (the seam count; seam 2 is a coordinated 3-touch). MagiComponents has ONE producer (taxOverlay.ts:952) fed by ONE nonSSordinary (:939); seams 3/4/5 read it. The taxable vector is added at SEAM 2 ONLY (editing seam 3 separately double-counts the §86 base). The explicit edits are two seams (seam 1 cash netting, seam 2 ordinary income); seam 2 is three coordinated touches: a new TaxInputs.income field, threading per-year taxable into GrossUpContext (:1513-1523), and the + taxable at :939. A test proves the §86 provisional moved by the single (non-doubled) amount, realizedGain ≠ 0.

KTD-2 (the deflation math is NET-NEW). real-flat → emit the flat real value; nominal-flat / fixed-pct → real[t] = annualRealToday · (1+colaPct)^t / (1+inflation)^t using the deterministic inflation point estimate (0.03). The per-year vector builder shares NO structure with escalateQuote (write it fresh; borrow only nonZero). Correctness golden-gated (KTD-5). Viz corollary: a nominal-flat stream is a deterministic real curve (zero variance) — a DETERMINISTIC FLOOR in the confidence band, not a sampled spread (flag for U6/D2).

KTD-3 (two shapes — persisted entity vs compiled leaf). The PERSISTED IncomeStream entity is a new list incomeStreams on ScenarioV3 + SCENARIO_V3_FIELDS + the ties + init []. The COMPILED leaf PersonIncomeStream (the two death-state variants) wraps in IncomeParams on OverlayParams.income and is NEVER persisted (fidelity-over-duplication). R40 does NOT touch scenarioCodec.ts; U8 owns the v3 arm AND a real validation contract.

items.claim: KTD-4 (two pre-weighted variants, per-OWNER death-gated, zero-alloc select). Pre-compute TWO per-person variants at compile time — {grossFull, taxableFull} = Σ streams and {grossSurvivor, taxableSurvivor} = Σ streams·survivorPct (each with COLA/deflation + start/end gating baked in; survivor derived PER-STREAM, not as a scalar reweight of FULL). The death-dependent select is the only path-loop work, in a helper ongoingIncomeForYear that mirrors the death-gate STRUCTURE of contributionsForYear — NOT its allocation profile: it returns TWO household scalars, accumulating in the people loop with NO new Array, NO wrapper object, NO per-year offsets.some()/.find() (integer comparisons against the locked deathOffsets only). Per OWNER: select = (t < deathOffsets[ownerIdx]) ? FULL : (survivorAlive ? SURVIVOR : 0); survivorAlive = otherIdx exists && t < deathOffsets[otherIdx]; single-person ⇒ post-death branch 0. Locked at the death offset, never ramped; death gate only (never t < o.retire). Death-before-start is free (the SURVIVOR variant is 0 until the start year, then survivorPct·value). Each person's bundle is INDEPENDENTLY gated on that person's OWN death — a single household-level death gate is the bug a swap-mutant must catch (Unit 3).

KTD-4 corollary (entity-side range gate): survivorPct/taxableFraction are scalars on the ENTITY, applied at compile and multiplied away — they do NOT exist on the compiled leaf, so the engine CANNOT range-check them. That range gate lives at the entity boundary — KTD-3 / Unit 4 sanity / the restore codec. This CORRECTS the scoping doc's over-claim that the engine validateParams range-checks them.
items.duplicatedIn: System-Wide Impact (Validation boundary); Risks; Superseded section

items.claim: KTD-5 (golden-gated correctness). Every numeric claim is pinned by a hand-derived externally-computed golden, walked through its conditional fork with the pinned boundary named.

KTD-6 (taxableFraction selection; the tax-treatment inputs are a DISCRIMINATED UNION keyed on type). Model the tax-treatment fields as a discriminated union on type (mirror TickerClassification), so a pension entity cannot carry annuity-exclusion fields and an alimony entity cannot carry a contradictory direct taxableFraction — the contradiction is UNREPRESENTABLE in authored code. At restore it IS representable (JSON.parse + as erases the union) — so the codec must re-validate the full arm. The fork inputs are the source of truth; compileIncomeStreams derives the effective fraction (post-2018 alimony → 0; pre-2019 → 1; non-qual annuity → entered exclusion; qualified/pension/rental/other → entered/default fraction). No redundant derived fraction is persisted.

KTD-7 (survivor income-% and survivor spending-ratio modeled INDEPENDENTLY — confirmed). survivorSpendingRatio (0.75, a needs figure, fires on the first death of EITHER spouse) and survivorPct (a receipts figure, keyed to the OWNER's death) model different things and compose correctly at seam 1. The compound-widow test + the cross-owner-death-order test (Unit 3) prove no double-application and that the per-owner gating holds on the asymmetric death order.

KTD-8 (date-sweep + already-receiving). (a) Income is Y-INVARIANT → it passes through ...overlayBase un-truncated (do NOT add it to truncateStreams); perf corollary: compileIncomeStreams runs ONCE in buildParams, never in buildCandidateParams (the 4 compiled per-person vectors pass by reference). (b) startAge ≤ currentAge ⇒ already-receiving, CLAMP to t=0, never reject — compileIncomeStreams clamps start to max(0, startAge − currentAge); validateParams/sanity do NOT reject it. THE ANCHOR: for an already-receiving stream annualRealToday is the real value AT sim-year 0; the decay exponent is the clamped t, NEVER the stream's elapsed age (else a plausible 'honor the real age' impl over-deflates a real driver's pension). A golden pins gross[0] === annualRealToday.

KTD-9 (already-receiving × working-year IRMAA — STRUCTURAL DECOUPLE, not a copy control). Hazard: an already-receiving stream's taxable in a §7-clamped working year collides with the additive working-year override (override[t] + irmaaMagi(components)), and seam-2's unconditional add would also mint a phantom portfolio withdrawal to pay tax the wages already cover. A copy instruction ('enter your MAGI inclusive of all income') is NOT a sound control — a user entering wages-only would, with engine-side suppression, drop the pension from IRMAA entirely (the optimistic sin). DECISION: decouple the two feeds structurally. (1) Re-specify the working-year override as the WAGES / non-modeled-MAGI component ONLY, and INVERT the copy to 'enter your working-year income EXCLUDING anything you entered as a retirement income stream.' (2) The engine OWNS each modeled stream's IRMAA-MAGI contribution in ALL years (clamped and unclamped) — so IRMAA-MAGI for a clamped working year is wages-override + the stream's own taxable, each counted exactly once. (3) In a CLAMPED working year the stream's taxable feeds IRMAA-MAGI but NOT the gross-up netting — no phantom withdrawal. Tests pin: IRMAA = wages + pension counted once on the wages-only-entry path; and no portfolio withdrawal minted for an already-receiving pension's tax in a clamped working year.

items.claim: Open Questions resolved: ATC #1/#2/#3 (keep advanced tier; ship 'other'; add R40 entry) — YES. Note: 'other'/alimony/annuity are shipped because the engine supports them, but their guided-path questions + optimistic disclosures are TYPE-GATED so a rental/pension-only user never pays for them (Unit 4). The 'it's free' rationale is an engine truth, not a product one; the identity fence is the bound.

Open Questions resolved: Sequencing — keep the build order; R40's Unit 4 intake is session-only until U8 (the next build), consistent with the accounts intake; Unit 4 adds a 'nothing's saved yet' affordance (option a). Net-rental cliff-compound — disclose the cliff MAGNITUDE + a fixture (option A); the modest-real-rise upgrade (option B) is noted, deferred behind BLS rent-CAGR verification. Rental survivor-% — broaden the no-safe-default survivor-% surfacing to pension/annuity/rental/other (alimony stays 0 by law).

The CRITICAL 'non-taxable income is ACA-MAGI wage-blind' finding — REJECTED as a false alarm. R40 non-taxable income (post-2018 alimony, annuity return-of-basis) genuinely is NOT federal MAGI and genuinely reduces withdrawal need — a lower MAGI → higher subsidy is the TRUE answer (real ACA planning leans on non-taxable income to stay under the cliff). The taxable portion DOES hit MAGI via seam 2; no income source 'should raise MAGI but doesn't.' Value retained: the Unit 3 'non-taxable moves none of the MAGIs' test ALSO asserts the ACA subsidy correctly RISES (the A1 confirmation).

(absent ≡ lifetime — NEVER numeric/Infinity sentinel), colaMode ∈ COLA_MODES, colaPct?, survivorPct, + discriminated-union tax-treatment keyed on type }. PersonIncomeStream (compiled leaf) = { grossFull?, taxableFull?, grossSurvivor?, taxableSurvivor? } — optional per-year readonly number[], auxiliary. IncomeParams = { readonly incomeByPerson: readonly PersonIncomeStream[] }, index-aligned to people. OverlayParams.income? optional — presence is the reduce-to-spine key.

Unit 2: intakeMap compilation — the two variants, the net-new COLA math, the goldens. Requirements R40.3/.10, KTD-2/4/5/6/8. Files: src/intake/intakeMap.ts (compileIncomeStreams(d, ownerIndex, horizonYears) → one person's PersonIncomeStream; the per-type default table); create only if a default COLA-rate hint is shown: src/intake/referenceData.ts entry; test src/intake/__tests__/incomeCompile.test.ts. Per stream per year t: gross[t] per KTD-2, gated by startAge/endAge, start clamped to max(0, startAge − currentAge) with annualRealToday anchored at t=0 (KTD-8b); taxable[t] = gross[t] · effectiveFraction (KTD-6). Sum into FULL (Σ gross, Σ taxable) and SURVIVOR (Σ gross·survivorPct, Σ taxable·survivorPct) PER-STREAM. Drop all-zero vectors via nonZero.

Unit 2 golden examples (DND/012, hand-derived): real-flat → flat; nominal-flat → geometric real-decay (e.g. $45k at 3% ≈ halves by ~year 23); fixed-pct → net-real-rate decay. Already-receiving anchor golden (KTD-8b): nominal-flat with startAge ≤ currentAge → gross[0] === annualRealToday AND gross[1] === annualRealToday/(1+infl). Survivor variant per-stream: two streams owned by one person, survivorPct 0.5 and 0 → grossSurvivor = 0.5·streamA + 0·streamB (asserts Σ streams·survivorPct, NOT 0.5·grossFull). Fork: post-2018 alimony → taxable=0; pre-2019 → taxable=gross; qualified annuity → 1; non-qual → entered exclusion.

Unit 3: The atomic engine integration — wire, validate, zero-alloc select, seam 1 + seam 2, the IRMAA decouple, reduce-to-spine. Requirements R40.4/.5/.6/.10, KTD-1/4/7/8/9. Files: intakeMap.ts (per-household assembly loop ONCE in buildParams; presence-keyed spread; re-specify workingYearIrmaaMagiByPerson as wages/non-modeled per KTD-9); simulate.ts (zero-alloc ongoingIncomeForYear select; cashTermsForYear returns { net, ss, incomeTaxable } — updating BOTH callers path loop :904 AND netWithdrawalForYear :281 + ~12 test sites; push incomeTaxableYears and spread into taxInputs; validateParams income block — VECTOR finiteness + ≤ ENGINE_MAX_DOLLAR only, NOT survivorPct/taxableFraction range; income passes through ...overlayBase un-truncated); taxOverlay.ts (TaxInputs.income field; thread per-year taxable into GrossUpContext; + taxable at nonSSordinary :939 — seam 2 only; KTD-9: in a clamped working year (bridgeYearMask[t]) income taxable feeds IRMAA-MAGI but is excluded from gross-up's nonSSordinary; update MagiComponents muni-landmine comment; do NOT copy the §6 ACA empty-overlap guard). Tests: reduceToSpine, magi, survivor, dateSearch, irmaa, validateParams.

Unit 3 Execution note: START with the reduce-to-spine byte-identity test (absent income) as a CHARACTERIZATION PIN before touching the seams. ongoingIncomeForYear mirrors the death-gate STRUCTURE of contributionsForYear (not its 4-array alloc): two household scalars, integer-comparison death branch, per-owner gating. A SIBLING, not a refactor-share (gate domains differ, insight 027). Fold into the deferred hot-loop pass alongside the two survivor-recompute sites. Seam 1: net = max(0, spending − earned − ongoingIncomeGross − ss); do not collapse the double allocateWithdrawal. validateParams income block: length-tie; finiteness-first per entry; per-year assembled-sum finiteness; ≤ ENGINE_MAX_DOLLAR; startAge < currentAge ALLOWED.

Unit 3 test scenarios (discriminating): Reduce-to-spine (029) absent ⇒ byte-identical, nonzero owner-distinct pairwise-distinct two-person income ⇒ terminal moves + swap-mutant fails. MAGI atomicity (KTD-1) fully-taxable lifts SS-taxable + acaMagi + irmaaMagi consistently, §86 provisional rose ONCE (realizedGain ≠ 0); non-taxable (post-2018 alimony) nets draw but moves none of MAGIs AND ACA subsidy correctly RISES (A1). IRMAA decouple (KTD-9): already-receiving pension + working spouse + Medicare lookback + wages-only override → IRMAA-MAGI = wages + pension once; NO portfolio withdrawal minted. Survivor (KTD-4, 040): owner dies — survivorPct>0 continues, =0 (alimony) stops, deferred-pension owner dies BEFORE start → survivor benefit from start year, both-dead ⇒ $0, single-person ⇒ 0. Cross-owner death order (KTD-7): two streams one per spouse, non-owner-of-X dies first → deceased's stream drops to survivorPct, survivor's own stays FULL, 0.75 step-down fired ONCE, single-household-death-gate swap-mutant FAILS. ACA boundary inside bridge (014) + rental cliff-compound assert disclosed direction holds. Date-search invariance (KTD-8a). validateParams: NaN/Infinity rejected finiteness-first, length≠people rejected, per-year sum over ENGINE_MAX_DOLLAR rejected, startAge < currentAge ACCEPTED. Gross-up re-probe (006/007) converges within GROSS_UP_MAX_PASSES.

Unit 4: Intake UX — the opt-in expander, the income row form, the surfaced fields, the interaction states, sanity, copy. Requirements R40.7/.8/.1/.2/.10, KTD-6/8b/9. Files: CREATE src/intake/OtherIncomeEntry.tsx (the row form — NAMED to avoid the existing incomeStep/workIncomeStep earned-income collision); modify questions.tsx (OtherIncomeStep/expander; the gate; StepDef.fields derivation; 'not saved yet' affordance; section label 'other income (in retirement)'); intakeMap.ts (missingRequiredFacts pushes for surfaced no-safe-default fields); sanity.ts (incomeStreamField helper + entity-scalar range rules survivorPct/taxableFraction ∈ [0,1]; NO startAge < currentAge rule); src/ui/copy.ts (plain-language keys; slots.incomeSummary; disclosure lines; the INVERTED KTD-9 working-MAGI instruction; not-saved-yet line — all amount-free in violation/error strings); tests incomeIntake.test.ts + extend copyFence.test.ts.

Unit 4 UI law: any user-facing surface here is governed by back-nine-design (color is NEVER the only signal — Briggsy is color-blind; the not-saved-yet treatment is neutral text + icon, never a red badge), compound-engineering:frontend-design (direction), emil-design-eng (motion), web-design-guidelines (review) before touching .tsx. The disclosure copy is an N=1 cold-read deliverable.

Unit 4 interaction states (design-lens spec): Opt-in expander (mirror AccountsStep empty→Add→form), NOT auto-inserted. Section label 'other income (in retirement)', distinct from earned-income steps. The no-safe-default fields are IN-FORM, required-to-save (NOT a deferred push) — picking a type chip reveals its required field immediately, ABOVE the collapsed advanced tier, the row's Add button gated until answered (mirror AccountEntry.save() early-return): pension/annuity/rental/other → survivor-% prompt ('what happens to it if {spouse} passes first?', default empty, never 100%); alimony → post-2018 agreement-date. missingRequiredFacts is the BACKSTOP for a restored/edited row, not the primary surface. Advanced-tier rule: required-to-be-correct fields (survivor-%, alimony date) are NEVER in the collapsed tier; the collapsed tier holds only genuinely-optional refinements (end age, explicit COLA rate, exclusion fraction) with safe type-seeded defaults; colaPct is form-required when colaMode='fixed-pct' (conditional reveal within the tier).

Unit 4: 'Already receiving' is an EXPLICIT TOGGLE that owns the start-age field's state (on → the field shows 'receiving now', not a clamped number; off is the default). The row summary reads 'receiving now' for that state. This is the detectable state KTD-9's wages-only override copy depends on. Row summary (slots.incomeSummary) surfaces load-bearing facts in PLAIN LANGUAGE — type · owner · amount · (start/'receiving now') · COLA-keeps-up-or-not · survivor ('keeps half if Jane passes' / 'stops if she passes' / 'no inflation increases') — never survivorPct: 0.5 or a 3-fact account shortcut that hides the widow's numbers. 'Not saved yet' affordance: a RESERVED STATIC SLOT (not injected on first add — insight 035), a NEUTRAL TEXT + ICON treatment (explicitly NOT a red badge — color-blind-safe, role=note not alert), routed through copy.ts, present whenever the section has ≥1 stream.

Unit 4 disclosure copy classification: (a) INLINE HELP (aria-describedby) for entry-affecting lines (the alimony date threshold; the inverted working-MAGI instruction); (b) ON-DEMAND DEPTH (a quiet 'how we model this') for the optimistic-direction modeling residuals (net-rent cliff-magnitude, exclusion-never-exhausts, alimony payer-death) + provenance lines (rental survivor = state property law, QJSA = plan-rep-or-notary, COLA norms = practitioner). These are an N=1 cold-read TONE deliverable — they must read as CONSERVATIVE MODELING CHOICES, not confessions of error. Two-tap remove (mirror questions.tsx:577-593); empty-state inherits the accounts pattern.

Unit 5: The R40 requirements entry — the contract amendment. Requirements R40.9. Dependencies Units 1–4 (soft — sequence last). Files: docs/product.md §7. Approach: ADDITIVE amendment (insight 018 — zero-removals): grep the superseded premise ('two income streams', 'no ongoing non-earned income', 'income stops at retirement'); edit only where genuinely superseded. The entry states: the generic per-person stream; the five types; the two-variant compilation; the two-explicit-edit MAGI integration (KTD-1) + the IRMAA structural decouple (KTD-9); survivor continuation at death (KTD-4); the OUT list WITH DIRECTIONS NAMED; the provenance corrections; the U8 obligation (a checkIncomeStreamV3 codec validator).

Status note (Unit 5): the R40 entry ALREADY LIVES in docs/product.md §7 (the doc-rebuild carried it forward). Unit 5's remaining work is to reconcile any superseded-premise lines the zero-removals grep surfaces, and to confirm the OUT-list / provenance / U8-obligation are all present.

System-Wide Impact — Forward landmines (two): (1) Bracket-fill / Roth-conversion sizing — income's taxable[t] consumes bracket-fill headroom; the Controls / Recommendation acts (sequencing + conversion) must NET it before sizing conversions or it over-converts. (2) The working-year IRMAA channel is re-specified by KTD-9 (wages/non-modeled only) — a future feed must respect that the engine owns modeled streams' IRMAA contribution.

System-Wide Impact — Performance: (a) the select helper is ZERO-ALLOC (two scalars; integer-comparison death branch); (b) the 4 income vectors are Y-INVARIANT → compileIncomeStreams runs ONCE in buildParams; (c) gross-up is a non-issue — income's taxable is an additive constant, does not raise k (k_sup ≈ 0.74) and stays inside ENGINE_MAX_DOLLAR where the ~113-pass bound is proven; (d) the death-state branch joins the deferred hot-loop pass alongside the two survivor-recompute sites.

System-Wide Impact — Validation boundary (security-lens correction): the engine validateParams validates the COMPILED VECTORS (finiteness + ≤ ENGINE_MAX_DOLLAR); the ENTITY SCALAR RANGES (survivorPct ∈ [0,1], taxableFraction ∈ [0,1]) are STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE from the multiplied-away leaf, so they live ONLY at the entity boundary: Unit 4 sanity on the intake path, AND the U8 checkIncomeStreamV3 codec validator on the restore path (a restored blob bypasses the form and validateParams can't see the scalars — so the codec arm is LOAD-BEARING, not redundant).

System-Wide Impact — Unchanged invariants (canonical in docs/architecture.md): single shared market draw / CRN; reduce-to-spine byte-identity; the double allocateWithdrawal; truncateStreams (income NOT added); the PersonContributionStreams path; checkPerson/the frozen legacy shape; scenarioCodec (untouched — U8's). PersonIncomeStream/IncomeParams are engine-facing derivations, NEVER persisted (fidelity-over-duplication); only the IncomeStream entity reaches ScenarioV3.

State lifecycle: incomeStreams joins ScenarioV3 now but is NOT persisted until U8 — the income intake (like accounts) is SESSION-ONLY; Unit 4 carries a 'not saved yet' affordance. NO IndexedDB write is added by R40. No net-new at-rest or network exposure — income never leaves the device; CSP connect-src 'self'. Error propagation: intake — missingRequiredFacts stops a half-entered stream; sanity range-gates entity scalars; engine validateParams finiteness-first on vectors. Restore — the codec is the sole semantic gate. All violation/rejection copy NAMES THE FIELD, NOT THE VALUE.

items.claim: Risks table mitigations (one-line each, all load-bearing): IRMAA double/under-count → KTD-9 structural decouple. Per-stream survivor-% lost by collapsing → KTD-4 two variants, golden derives grossSurvivor per-stream. Cross-owner death miscredits a dead spouse's pension → KTD-7/Unit 3 per-owner gating + cross-owner-death-order swap-mutant. Seam-3 double-count → KTD-1 seam 2 only, §86-moved-once test realizedGain ≠ 0. Engine cannot range-check survivorPct/taxableFraction → entity-side (Unit 4 sanity + U8 codec). Date-sweep zeroes a retiree's pension → KTD-8a un-truncated, compiled once. Already-retired pensioner false-rejected/mis-anchored → KTD-8b clamp to t=0, anchored at sim-year 0. Optimistic survivor floor → KTD-4 select locked at death offset, survivorAlive guards both-dead ⇒ $0. Net-rental real-flat compounds at ACA cliff → disclosed with magnitude + Unit 3 fixture. Rental ~100% survivor silent optimistic default → survivor-% surfacing broadened. Hot-loop alloc regression → zero-alloc two-scalar helper. Gross-up non-convergence → re-probe at SS-torpedo + bracket-fill corner (perf non-issue). Reduce-to-spine drift → characterization byte-identity pin first. Contradictory persisted entity → KTD-6 union + U8 codec re-validates full discriminant arm. Session-only data loss → sequencing option a + not-saved-yet affordance.

U8 hand-off obligation (the checkIncomeStreamV3 codec validator, importing the single-sourced vocab): finiteness-first; enum membership (needVocab); ownerIndex ∈ {0,1}; survivorPct/taxableFraction range (the SOLE restore-path gate); colaPct REQUIRED-and-finite when colaMode='fixed-pct' (absent/null = corruption, NEVER coerced to 0 — the optimistic-erosion direction); the full fork/type arm (each type's required fields present, contradictory absent — since JSON.parse + as erases the union); endAge absent ≡ lifetime (DND-009, no numeric sentinel). R40 single-sources INCOME_TYPES/COLA_MODES as const.

items.claim: Provenance corrections (do NOT mis-cite at build) — four claims the scoping pass attributed to the wrong primary: (1) Rental ~100% survivor rests on STATE PROPERTY LAW (JTWROS / community property), NOT IRS Pub 559/551 — cite to state law; only true if jointly owned / willed to the spouse. (2) Net rental ≠ real-flat: gross rent tracks inflation but the fixed-nominal depreciation shield erodes, so taxable net rent rises in real terms; v1 models net as real-flat as a disclosed simplification; verify the rent-CAGR figure against the BLS series before it goes load-bearing. (3) Pension QJSA consent can be witnessed by a PLAN REPRESENTATIVE OR a NOTARY — not strictly notarized (IRC 417(a)(2)) — copy must say so. (4) Alimony/pension/annuity COLA norms are PRACTITIONER/ECONOMIC facts, NOT IRS — label as such (no IRS section governs whether a decree or annuity has a COLA).

items.claim: Verified tax facts appendix — ALIMONY: post-2018 agreements not taxable to recipient / not deductible by payer (TCJA; Pub 504, Topic 452); pre-2019 taxable/deductible unless expressly modified; reported Sch 1 line 2a → AGI; terminates at recipient death (§71(b)(1)(D)) → 0% survivor.

Verified tax facts appendix — PENSION: fully ordinary taxable (1040 5b); Simplified Method gives a fixed-nominal tax-free basis portion that shrinks then stops (Pub 575); QJSA 50% federal floor; election single-life/50/75/100 (IRC 401(a)(11)/417); into AGI/MAGI → affects ACA/SS-taxation/IRMAA/Roth headroom. RENTAL: net (gross − expenses − depreciation, 27.5yr SL) ordinary on Sch E → AGI/MAGI; passive, no SE tax, continues past retirement until sold (Pub 527/925); recapture/cap-gains/step-up fire only on sale (OUT v1). ANNUITY: qualified = fully taxable; non-qualified = exclusion ratio (basis/expected-return, Pub 939; 26 CFR 1.72-4), tax-free until basis recovered then 100% taxable; fixed = flat nominal, COLA = optional rider that lowers initial payout; J&S survivor %; taxable portion → MAGI.
